title.zh: 卷七十八 志第五十四 食貨二
title.raw: 卷七十八 志第五十四 食貨二 Volume 78 Treatises 54: Finance and Economics 2

sentences.zh: 賦役之法，唐租庸調猶為近古。

translations.literal: As for the law of taxes and corvée, the Tang system's zu-yong-diao still came close to the ancient model.
translations.idiomatic: In matters of tax and corvée, the Tang practice of zu, yong, and diao still resembled the older order more closely than what followed.

sentences.zh: 自楊炎作兩稅法，簡而易行，歷代相沿，至明不改。

translations.literal: From when Yang Yan created the two-tax law, it was simple and easy to implement; successive dynasties followed it in succession, and up through the Ming it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Yan introduced the two-tax system, its simplicity and ease of administration won lasting adoption; dynasty after dynasty kept it, and the Ming did not alter it.

sentences.zh: 太祖為吳王，賦稅十取一，役法計田出夫。

translations.literal: When the Taizu was King of Wu, taxes were taken as one in ten, and the corvée law calculated laborers by field.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founding Emperor was still King of Wu, he levied taxes at one tenth, and apportioned corvée labor according to holdings in land.

sentences.zh: 縣上、中、下三等，以賦十萬、六萬、三萬石下為差。

translations.literal: Counties were graded upper, middle, and lower third class, differentiated by whether tax revenue fell below one hundred thousand, sixty thousand, or thirty thousand dan of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Counties ranked upper, middle, or lower based on whether their registered levies fell below one hundred thousand, sixty thousand, or thirty thousand dan.

sentences.zh: 府三等，以賦二十萬上下、十萬石下為差。

translations.literal: Prefectures were also in three grades, differentiated by whether tax revenue was above or below two hundred thousand or below one hundred thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures likewise fell into three grades, keyed to whether their levies stood above or below two hundred thousand dan, or below one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，定賦役法，一以黃冊為準。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his accession to the throne, he fixed the law of taxes and corvée, taking the yellow registers as the sole standard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his enthronement he codified tax and corvée law, with the yellow registers as the sole authority.

sentences.zh: 冊有丁有田，丁有役，田有租。

translations.literal: The registers recorded males and fields; males had corvée, fields had rent.
translations.idiomatic: The registers listed household males and land: males bore corvée duty, land bore grain rent.

sentences.zh: 租曰夏稅，曰秋糧，凡二等。

translations.literal: Rent was called summer tax and autumn grain, two categories in all.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax came in two forms: summer tax and autumn grain.

sentences.zh: 夏稅無過八月，秋糧無過明年二月。

translations.literal: Summer tax was not to extend past the eighth month; autumn grain not past the second month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax had to be paid by the eighth month at latest; autumn grain by the second month of the new year.

sentences.zh: 丁曰成丁，曰未成丁，凡二等。

translations.literal: Males were called adult males and non-adult males, two categories in all.
translations.idiomatic: Household males were classified as adults or minors—two grades in all.

sentences.zh: 民始生，籍其名曰不成丁，年十六曰成丁。

translations.literal: When the people were first born, they were registered by name as non-adult males; at age sixteen they were called adult males.
translations.idiomatic: Newborns were registered as minors; at sixteen they became liable adults.

sentences.zh: 成丁而役，六十而免。

translations.literal: Adult males performed corvée; at sixty they were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Adults performed corvée until age sixty, when they were released from duty.

sentences.zh: 又有職役優免者，役曰裏甲，曰均徭，曰雜泛，凡三等。

translations.literal: There were also those with official duties who received preferential exemption; corvée was called li-jia, equalized corvée, and miscellaneous levies, three categories in all.
translations.idiomatic: Certain officeholders enjoyed corvée exemptions. Duties fell into three kinds: li-jia service, equalized corvée, and miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 以戶計曰甲役，以丁計曰徭役，上命非時曰雜役，皆有力役，有僱役。

translations.literal: Calculated by household it was called jia service; calculated by male it was called yao corvée; commands from above not at the regular time were called miscellaneous corvée—all had labor corvée and hired corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Household-based duties were jia service; male-based duties were yao corvée; extraordinary imperial orders were miscellaneous corvée. Each category could be fulfilled by labor or by hired substitutes.

sentences.zh: 府州縣驗冊丁口多寡，事產厚薄，以均適其力。

translations.literal: Prefectures, subprefectures, and counties verified the registers for the number of males and the thickness or thinness of property, to equalize and suit their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures, subprefectures, and counties checked registers for household size and wealth, then apportioned burdens to match each taxpayer's capacity.

sentences.zh: 兩稅，洪武時，夏稅曰米麥，曰錢鈔，曰絹。

translations.literal: Under the two taxes, in the Hongwu period summer tax was called rice and wheat, paper money, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Under the two-tax system in the Hongwu reign, summer tax was paid in grain, paper notes, or silk.

sentences.zh: 秋糧曰米，曰錢鈔，曰絹。

translations.literal: Autumn grain was called rice, paper money, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn grain likewise could be paid in rice, paper notes, or silk.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，會計之數，夏稅曰大小米麥，曰麥荍，曰絲綿並荒絲，曰稅絲，曰絲綿折絹，曰稅絲折絹，曰本色絲，曰農桑絲折絹，曰農桑零絲，曰人丁絲折絹，曰改科絹，曰棉花折布，曰薴布，曰土薴，曰紅花，曰麻布，曰鈔，曰租鈔，曰稅鈔，曰原額小絹，曰幣帛絹，曰本色絹，曰絹，曰折色絲。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period, the accounting categories for summer tax included large and small rice and wheat, wheat and chaff, silk floss together with waste silk, tax silk, silk floss converted to silk fabric, tax silk converted to silk fabric, silk in kind, farm-and-mulberry silk converted to silk fabric, farm-and-mulberry loose silk, per-capita silk converted to silk fabric, reclassified silk fabric, cotton converted to cloth, ramie cloth, native ramie, safflower, hemp cloth, paper notes, rent notes, tax notes, original-quota small silk, currency silk, silk in kind, silk fabric, and converted-color silk.
translations.idiomatic: By the Hongzhi reign the summer-tax ledger had grown elaborate: grain and wheat in several grades, chaff, silk floss and waste silk, tax silk, floss and tax silk commuted to fabric, silk paid in kind, farm-mulberry silk and loose ends, per-capita silk, reclassified silk, cotton and ramie commuted to cloth, native ramie, safflower, hemp cloth, various paper notes, small silk at original quotas, currency silk, and commuted silk of every description.

sentences.zh: 秋糧曰米，曰租鈔，曰賃鈔，曰山租鈔，曰租絲，曰租絹，曰粗租麻布，曰課程棉布，曰租薴布，曰牛租米穀，曰地畝棉花絨，曰棗子易米，曰棗株課米，曰課程薴麻折米，曰棉布，曰魚課米，曰改科絲折米。

translations.literal: Autumn grain was called rice, rent notes, lease notes, mountain-rent notes, rent silk, rent silk fabric, coarse-rent hemp cloth, course cotton cloth, rent ramie cloth, ox-rent grain, per-mu cotton floss, jujubes exchanged for rice, jujube-tree levy rice, course ramie and hemp converted to rice, cotton cloth, fish-levy rice, and reclassified silk converted to rice.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn grain entries likewise multiplied: rice, rent and lease notes, mountain-rent notes, rent silk and fabric, coarse hemp and course cotton, ramie cloth, ox-rent grain, cotton floss by the mu, jujube levies commuted to rice, ramie and hemp courses, cotton cloth, fish levies, and reclassified silk—all reckoned against the autumn quota.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，小有所增損，大略以米麥為主，而絲絹與鈔次之。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period there were small additions and subtractions; broadly speaking rice and wheat were primary, while silk fabric and paper notes came next.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli the categories shifted slightly, but grain remained primary and silk and paper notes secondary.

sentences.zh: 夏稅之米惟江西、湖廣、廣東、廣西，麥荍惟貴州，農桑絲遍天下，惟不及川、廣、雲、貴，餘各視其地產。

translations.literal: Summer-tax rice was only in Jiangxi, Huguang, Guangdong, and Guangxi; wheat and chaff only in Guizhou; farm-and-mulberry silk throughout the realm, only not reaching Sichuan, Guang, Yunnan, and Guizhou; the rest each according to local products.
translations.idiomatic: Summer tax in rice applied chiefly to Jiangxi, Huguang, Guangdong, and Guangxi; wheat and chaff chiefly to Guizhou; farm-mulberry silk nearly everywhere except Sichuan, Guang, Yunnan, and Guizhou; other items followed local production.

sentences.zh: 太祖初立國即下令，凡民田五畝至十畝者，栽桑、麻、木棉各半畝，十畝以上倍之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu first established the state he immediately issued an order: for all civilian fields from five to ten mu, plant mulberry, hemp, and cotton each half a mu; for ten mu and above, double it.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the dynasty was founded, the Taizu ordered that holdings of five to ten mu plant half a mu each of mulberry, hemp, and cotton, and holdings above ten mu plant double that amount.

sentences.zh: 麻畝徵八兩，木棉畝四兩。

translations.literal: Hemp was levied eight taels per mu; cotton four taels per mu.
translations.idiomatic: The levy was eight taels of hemp per mu and four taels of cotton per mu.

sentences.zh: 栽桑以四年起科。

translations.literal: Mulberry planting began taxation after four years.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry plots began to bear tax after four years.

sentences.zh: 不種桑，出絹一疋。

translations.literal: If one did not plant mulberry, one paid one bolt of silk fabric.
translations.idiomatic: Households that failed to plant mulberry paid one bolt of silk instead.

sentences.zh: 不種麻及木棉，出麻布、棉布各一疋。

translations.literal: If one did not plant hemp and cotton, one paid one bolt each of hemp cloth and cotton cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to plant hemp or cotton required payment of one bolt of hemp cloth and one bolt of cotton cloth.

sentences.zh: 此農桑絲絹所由起也。

translations.literal: This was how farm-and-mulberry silk and fabric arose.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the origins of the farm-mulberry silk and fabric levies.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，天下稅糧，令民以銀、鈔、錢、絹代輸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongwu, for tax grain throughout the realm, the people were ordered to substitute payment with silver, paper notes, cash, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 9 the court allowed taxpayers nationwide to remit grain taxes in silver, paper notes, cash, or silk.

sentences.zh: 銀一兩、錢千文、鈔一貫，皆折輸米一石，小麥則減直十之二。

translations.literal: One tael of silver, one thousand cash, or one string of paper notes—all were converted to pay one dan of rice; for wheat the valuation was reduced by two tenths.
translations.idiomatic: One tael of silver, one thousand cash, or one string of notes each commuted to one dan of rice; wheat was valued at twenty percent less.

sentences.zh: 棉薴一疋，折米六斗，麥七斗。

translations.literal: One bolt of cotton or ramie cloth was converted to six dou of rice or seven dou of wheat.
translations.idiomatic: A bolt of cotton or ramie cloth counted as six dou of rice or seven dou of wheat.

sentences.zh: 麻布一疋，折米四斗，麥五斗。

translations.literal: One bolt of hemp cloth was converted to four dou of rice or five dou of wheat.
translations.idiomatic: A bolt of hemp cloth commuted to four dou of rice or five dou of wheat.

sentences.zh: 絲絹等各以輕重為損益，願人粟者聽。

translations.literal: Silk and fabric each were increased or decreased according to weight; those who wished to deliver grain were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Silk and fabric conversions varied by weight, and those who preferred to pay grain directly were allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 十七年，雲南以金、銀、貝、布、漆、丹砂、水銀代秋租。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Yunnan used gold, silver, cowrie shells, cloth, lacquer, cinnabar, and mercury in place of autumn rent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 Yunnan was permitted to pay autumn rent in gold, silver, cowries, cloth, lacquer, cinnabar, and mercury.

sentences.zh: 於是謂米麥為本色，而諸折納稅糧者，謂之折色。

translations.literal: Thereupon rice and wheat were called payment in kind, while all tax grain paid by conversion were called commuted payment.
translations.idiomatic: Hence rice and wheat paid in kind were called ben payment, and all commuted dues were called zhe payment.

sentences.zh: 越二年，又令戶部侍郎楊靖會計天下倉儲存糧，二年外並收折色，惟北方諸布政司需糧餉邊，仍使輸粟。

translations.literal: Two years later, he again ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Jing to tally stored grain in granaries throughout the realm; beyond two years' supply all was collected as commuted payment, only the northern provincial commissions needing grain for border provisions still had grain delivered.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Vice Minister Yang Jing audited granary stocks empire-wide: wherever stores exceeded two years' supply, commuted payment was accepted; only northern commissions feeding the frontier still required grain in kind.

sentences.zh: 三十年諭戶部曰：「行人高稹言，陝西困逋賦。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he instructed the Ministry of Revenue, saying: The traveling clerk Gao Zhi says Shaanxi is distressed by arrears in tax.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 he told the Ministry of Revenue: "The traveling clerk Gao Zhi reports that Shaanxi is crushed by tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 其議自二十八年以前，天下逋租，咸許任土所產，折收布、絹、棉花及金、銀等物，著為令。

translations.literal: Let it be discussed that from before the twenty-eighth year, arrears in rent throughout the realm may all be permitted according to local products, collected in conversion as cloth, silk, cotton, and gold, silver, and other items, and established as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Consider allowing all rent arrears from before year 28 to be settled in local products—cloth, silk, cotton, gold, silver, and the like—and codify this as law."

sentences.zh: 」於是戶部定：鈔一錠，折米一石；

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Ministry of Revenue fixed: one ingot of paper notes converted to one dan of rice;
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry then set commutation rates: one ingot of paper notes for one dan of rice;

sentences.zh: 金一兩，十石；

translations.literal: one tael of gold, ten dan;
translations.idiomatic: one tael of gold for ten dan;

sentences.zh: 銀一兩，二石；

translations.literal: one tael of silver, two dan;
translations.idiomatic: one tael of silver for two dan;

sentences.zh: 絹一疋，石有二斗；

translations.literal: one bolt of silk fabric, one dan and two dou;
translations.idiomatic: one bolt of silk for one dan and two dou;

sentences.zh: 棉布一疋，一石；

translations.literal: one bolt of cotton cloth, one dan;
translations.idiomatic: one bolt of cotton cloth for one dan;

sentences.zh: 薴布一疋，七斗；

translations.literal: one bolt of ramie cloth, seven dou;
translations.idiomatic: one bolt of ramie cloth for seven dou;

sentences.zh: 棉花一斤，二斗。

translations.literal: one jin of cotton, two dou.
translations.idiomatic: one jin of raw cotton for two dou.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「折收逋賦，蓋欲蘇民困也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: Collecting arrears by conversion is meant to relieve the people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Commuting arrears is meant to ease the people's hardship.

sentences.zh: 今賦重若此，將愈困民，豈恤之之意哉。

translations.literal: Now if the tax burden is this heavy, it will only further distress the people—how is this the intent to show compassion?
translations.idiomatic: Rates this heavy will only crush them further. Is this what compassion looks like?

sentences.zh: 金、銀每兩折米加一倍。

translations.literal: For gold and silver, each tael's conversion to rice was doubled.
translations.idiomatic: He doubled the grain equivalent for each tael of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 鈔止二貫五百文折一石。

translations.literal: Paper notes were limited to two strings and five hundred cash for one dan.
translations.idiomatic: Paper notes were set at two strings and five hundred cash per dan.

sentences.zh: 餘從所議。」

translations.literal: The rest followed what had been proposed."
translations.idiomatic: Everything else followed the original proposal."

sentences.zh: 永樂中，既得交阯，以絹，漆，蘇木，翠羽，紙扇，沉、速、安息諸香代租賦。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period, once Jiaozhi had been taken, silk, lacquer, sappanwood, kingfisher feathers, paper fans, and aloeswood, sandalwood, and various benzoin incenses were used in place of rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle conquered Jiaozhi, rent and tax there were paid in silk, lacquer, sappanwood, kingfisher feathers, paper fans, and assorted aromatics including aloes, sandalwood, and benzoin.

sentences.zh: 廣東瓊州黎人、肇慶瑤人內附，輸賦比內地。

translations.literal: The Li people of Qiongzhou in Guangdong and the Yao people of Zhaoqing who submitted inward paid taxes comparable to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When the Li of Qiongzhou and the Yao of Zhaoqing in Guangdong submitted, their tax obligations matched those of the interior.

sentences.zh: 天下本色稅糧三千餘萬石，絲鈔等二千餘萬。

translations.literal: Tax grain in kind throughout the realm was more than thirty million dan; silk, paper notes, and the like more than twenty million.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide grain tax in kind exceeded thirty million dan; silk, notes, and commuted dues totaled more than twenty million units.

sentences.zh: 計是時，宇內富庶，賦入盈羨，米粟自輸京師數百萬石外，府縣倉廩蓄積甚豐，至紅腐不可食。

translations.literal: Considering that time, within the four seas there was wealth and plenty; tax revenue overflowed. Apart from several million dan of grain and millet delivered to the capital on their own, prefectural and county granaries stored accumulations so abundant that they rotted red and could not be eaten.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was prosperous and revenues abundant. Besides the millions of dan shipped to the capital, prefectural and county granaries overflowed until grain rotted red and inedible.

sentences.zh: 歲歉，有司往往先發粟振貸，然後以聞。

translations.literal: In years of poor harvest, the responsible officials often first issued grain for relief and loans, then reported afterward.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years officials often distributed relief grain and seed loans first and reported to the throne afterward.

sentences.zh: 雖歲貢銀三十萬兩有奇，而民間交易用銀，仍有厲禁。

translations.literal: Although the annual tribute of silver was more than three hundred thousand taels, yet for the people's private transactions using silver there were still strict prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Though annual silver tribute exceeded three hundred thousand taels, private silver trade among the people remained strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖定天下官、民田賦，凡官田畝稅五升三合五勺，民田減二升，重租田八升五合五勺，沒官田一斗二升。

translations.literal: At first, when the Taizu fixed taxes on official and civilian fields throughout the realm, in general official fields paid five sheng three he five shao per mu, civilian fields two sheng less, heavy-rent fields eight sheng five he five shao, and confiscated official fields one dou two sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu first set land tax empire-wide, official land paid five sheng three he five shao per mu, civilian land two sheng less, heavy-rent land eight sheng five he five shao, and confiscated official land one dou two sheng.

sentences.zh: 惟蘇、鬆、嘉、湖，怒其為張士誠守，乃籍諸豪族及富民田以為官田，按私租簿為稅額。

translations.literal: Only for Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, angry that they had held out for Zhang Shicheng, he registered the fields of powerful clans and wealthy households as official fields, using private rent ledgers as the tax quota.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou alone were punished for holding out for Zhang Shicheng: elite and wealthy holdings were registered as official land and taxed at private-rent rates recorded in ledgers.

sentences.zh: 而司農卿楊憲又以浙西地膏腴，增其賦，畝加二倍。

translations.literal: Moreover Minister of Agriculture Yang Xian, because the land of western Zhejiang was fertile and rich, increased their tax, doubling it per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Agriculture Yang Xian then doubled per-mu rates across western Zhejiang on grounds of its exceptional fertility.

sentences.zh: 故浙西官、民田視他方倍蓰，畝稅有二三石者。

translations.literal: Therefore official and civilian fields in western Zhejiang were several times those elsewhere; per-mu tax reached two or three dan in some cases.
translations.idiomatic: Western Zhejiang's official and civilian rates thus ran several times higher than elsewhere, with per-mu levies reaching two or three dan.

sentences.zh: 大抵蘇最重，鬆、嘉、湖次之，常、杭又次之。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking Suzhou was heaviest, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou next, Changzhou and Hangzhou after that.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou bore the heaviest burden, followed by Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, then Changzhou and Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武十三年命戶部裁其額，畝科七斗五升至四斗四升者減十之二，四斗三升至三斗六升者俱止徵三斗五升，其以下者仍舊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongwu he ordered the Ministry of Revenue to trim their quotas: where per-mu levy was from seven dou five sheng down to four dou four sheng, reduce by two tenths; from four dou three sheng down to three dou six sheng, all stop at levying three dou five sheng; below that, remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 13 the ministry trimmed quotas: rates from seven dou five sheng down to four dou four sheng were cut twenty percent; from four dou three sheng down to three dou six sheng were capped at three dou five sheng; lower rates stayed unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時蘇州一府，秋糧二百七十四萬六千餘石，自民糧十五萬石外，皆官田糧。

translations.literal: At that time one prefecture, Suzhou, had autumn grain of two million seven hundred forty-six thousand-odd dan; apart from one hundred fifty thousand dan of civilian grain, all was official-field grain.
translations.idiomatic: Even after trimming, Suzhou prefecture alone owed more than 2.74 million dan of autumn grain—only 150,000 dan of it civilian tax, the rest official-field rent.

sentences.zh: 官糧歲額與浙江通省埒，其重猶如此。

translations.literal: The annual quota of official grain equaled that of Zhejiang province as a whole; the burden was still this heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou's official-grain quota alone matched all of Zhejiang province—such was the burden's scale.

sentences.zh: 建文二年詔曰：「江、浙賦獨重，而蘇、鬆準私租起科，特以懲一時頑民，豈可為定則以重困一方。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwen an edict said: Jiang and Zhe taxes alone are heavy, while Suzhou and Songjiang were assessed according to private rent—this was solely to punish the stubborn people of the moment. How can it be made a fixed rule to heavily distress one region?
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwen year 2 an edict declared: "Jiang and Zhe taxes are uniquely heavy; Suzhou and Songjiang were assessed at private-rent rates only to punish those who had resisted. Such punishment cannot become a permanent rule that crushes a whole region.

sentences.zh: 宜悉與減免，畝不得過一斗。

translations.literal: All should be given reduction and exemption; per mu must not exceed one dou.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce and exempt them all; no holding may be taxed above one dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 」成祖盡革建文政，浙西之賦復重。

translations.literal: " The Chengzu completely abolished Jianwen policies, and western Zhejiang's taxes became heavy again.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengzu reversed Jianwen's reforms, and western Zhejiang's taxes grew heavy again.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，廣西布政使周幹巡視蘇、常、嘉、湖諸府還，言：「諸府民多逃亡，詢之耆老，皆云重賦所致。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong took the throne, Guangxi Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhou Gan, returning from inspecting the prefectures of Suzhou, Changzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, said: In these prefectures many of the people have fled. Inquiring of the elders, all said it was caused by heavy taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Xuanzong's accession, Guangxi commissioner Zhou Gan reported after touring Suzhou, Changzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou: "Mass flight afflicts these prefectures. Elders unanimously blame crushing tax burdens.

sentences.zh: 如吳江、崑山民田租，舊畝五升，小民佃種富民田，畝輸私租一石。

translations.literal: For example, civilian-field rent in Wujiang and Kunshan was formerly five sheng per mu; common people tenanting wealthy households' fields paid private rent of one dan per mu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wujiang and Kunshan civilian land once paid five sheng per mu, but tenants on wealthy landlords' fields paid private rent of one dan per mu.

sentences.zh: 後因事故入官，輒如私租例盡取之。

translations.literal: Later, when through some incident land entered official status, they would at once take it all according to the private-rent precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When such land later passed to the state, officials collected the full private-rent rate.

sentences.zh: 十分取八，民猶不堪，況盡取乎。

translations.literal: Taking eight out of ten, the people still could not bear it—how much less taking all?
translations.idiomatic: Eight parts in ten already broke them—what if the state took everything?

sentences.zh: 盡取，則民必凍餒，欲不逃亡，不可得也。

translations.literal: If all is taken, the people will surely freeze and starve; to wish them not to flee is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Full extraction would leave them freezing and starving; flight would be inevitable.

sentences.zh: 仁和、海寧、崑山海水陷官、民田千九百餘頃，逮今十有餘年，猶徵其租。

translations.literal: In Renhe, Haining, and Kunshan more than nineteen hundred qing of official and civilian fields were submerged by seawater; down to today, more than ten years later, rent is still levied.
translations.idiomatic: At Renhe, Haining, and Kunshan seawater had swallowed more than 1,900 qing of official and civilian land, yet rent was still collected after more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 田沒於海，租從何出？

translations.literal: Fields submerged in the sea—from where is rent to come?
translations.idiomatic: When fields lie beneath the sea, whence can rent come?

sentences.zh: 請將沒官田及公、侯還官田租，俱視彼處官田起科，畝稅六斗。

translations.literal: I request that rent on confiscated official fields and on fields returned to official status by dukes and marquises all be assessed like official fields there, six dou per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Please assess confiscated official land and land returned from noble estates at the local official-field rate of six dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 海水淪陷田，悉除其稅，則田無荒蕪之患，而細民獲安生矣。

translations.literal: For fields lost to seawater, completely remove their tax, then fields will have no worry of lying waste, and the common people will obtain secure livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Exempt all seawater-lost fields entirely, and wasteland will cease while commoners may live in peace.

sentences.zh: 」帝命部議行之。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered the ministry to discuss and implement it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered the ministries to deliberate and carry this out.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年二月詔：「舊額官田租，畝一斗至四斗者各減十之二，四斗一升至一石以上者減十之三。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Xuande an edict said: For old-quota official-field rent from one dou to four dou per mu, each reduce by two tenths; from four dou one sheng up to one dan and above, reduce by three tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5, month 2, an edict ordered: official-field rent at one to four dou per mu was cut twenty percent; from four dou one sheng up to one dan or more, thirty percent.

sentences.zh: 著為令。

translations.literal: Establish it as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: This was codified as law.

sentences.zh: 」於是江南巡撫周忱與蘇州知府況鐘，曲計減蘇糧七十餘萬，他府以為差，而東南民力少紓矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Jiangnan grand coordinator Zhou Chen and Suzhou prefect Kuang Zhong, by ingenious calculation reduced Suzhou grain by more than seven hundred thousand, other prefectures proportionally, and the people's strength in the southeast was somewhat relieved.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Coordinator Zhou Chen and Suzhou Prefect Kuang Zhong then engineered further cuts of more than 700,000 dan for Suzhou and proportional relief elsewhere, easing the southeast somewhat.

sentences.zh: 忱又令松江官田依民田起科，戶部劾以變亂成法。

translations.literal: Zhou Chen also ordered Songjiang official fields to be assessed like civilian fields; the Ministry of Revenue impeached him for altering established law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen also tried to assess Songjiang official land at civilian rates; the Ministry of Revenue impeached him for overturning established law.

sentences.zh: 宣宗雖不罪，亦不能從。

translations.literal: Although the Xuanzong did not punish him, he also could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong declined to punish him but could not approve the change.

sentences.zh: 而朝廷數下詔書，蠲除租賦。

translations.literal: Yet the court repeatedly issued edicts remitting rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: The court meanwhile issued repeated edicts remitting rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 持籌者輒私戒有司，勿以詔書為辭。

translations.literal: Those who held the counting rods would privately warn the responsible officials not to use the edicts as an excuse.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue officials privately warned local magistrates not to cite imperial remissions as grounds for reduction.

sentences.zh: 帝與尚書胡濙言：「計臣壅遏膏澤」，然不深罪也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Minister Hu Ying: The planners are damming up the imperial bounty—but he did not deeply punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Minister Hu Ying that revenue planners were blocking imperial relief, yet he did not punish them severely.

sentences.zh: 正統元年令蘇、鬆、浙江等處官田，準民田起科，秋糧四斗一升至二石以上者減作三斗，二斗一升以上至四斗者減作二斗，一斗一升至二斗者減作一斗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong he ordered that in Suzhou, Songjiang, Zhejiang, and other places official fields be assessed like civilian fields: autumn grain from four dou one sheng up to two dan and above was reduced to three dou; from two dou one sheng up to four dou, reduced to two dou; from one dou one sheng up to two dou, reduced to one dou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 1 official land in Suzhou, Songjiang, Zhejiang, and elsewhere was reassessed like civilian land: autumn rates from four dou one sheng up to two dan or more were cut to three dou; from two dou one sheng to four dou, to two dou; from one dou one sheng to two dou, to one dou.

sentences.zh: 蓋宣德末，蘇州逋糧至七百九十萬石，民困極矣。

translations.literal: For at the end of Xuande, Suzhou's arrears in grain reached seven million nine hundred thousand dan; the people were extremely distressed.
translations.idiomatic: By late Xuande Suzhou's grain arrears had reached 7.9 million dan and the people were at breaking point.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃獲少蘇。

translations.literal: Only then did they obtain slight relief.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did they gain a little relief.

sentences.zh: 英宗復闢之初，令鎮守浙江尚書孫原貞等定杭、嘉、湖則例，以起科重者徵米宜少，起科輕者徵米宜多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingzong's restoration to the throne, he ordered the minister guarding Zhejiang, Sun Yuanzhen, and others to fix the rate precedents for Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou: where initial assessment was heavy, grain collected per dan should be less; where initial assessment was light, grain collected should be more.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingzong's restoration, Minister Sun Yuanzhen guarding Zhejiang was told to set rates for Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou so that heavily assessed land paid less grain per nominal dan and lightly assessed land paid more.

sentences.zh: 乃定官田畝科一石以下，民田七斗以下者，每石歲徵平米一石三斗；

translations.literal: They then fixed: for official fields assessed below one dan per mu and civilian fields below seven dou, each dan annually collected was levied as one dan three dou of evened grain;
translations.idiomatic: They ruled that where official land was assessed below one dan per mu or civilian land below seven dou, each nominal dan owed 1.3 dan of evened grain annually;

sentences.zh: 官民田四斗以下者，每石歲徵平米一石五斗；

translations.literal: for official and civilian fields below four dou per mu, each dan annually collected one dan five dou of evened grain;
translations.idiomatic: where either was assessed below four dou per mu, each nominal dan owed 1.5 dan;

sentences.zh: 官田二斗以下，民田二斗七升以下者，每石歲徵平米一石七斗；

translations.literal: for official fields below two dou and civilian fields below two dou seven sheng, each dan annually one dan seven dou of evened grain;
translations.idiomatic: where official land was below two dou per mu or civilian below two dou seven sheng, each nominal dan owed 1.7 dan;

sentences.zh: 官田八升以下，民田七升以下者，每石歲徵平米二石二斗。

translations.literal: for official fields below eight sheng and civilian fields below seven sheng, each dan annually two dan two dou of evened grain.
translations.idiomatic: where official land was below eight sheng per mu or civilian below seven sheng, each nominal dan owed 2.2 dan.

sentences.zh: 凡重者輕之，輕者重之，欲使科則適均，而畝科一石之稅未嘗減云。

translations.literal: In general the heavy were lightened and the light were weighted, intending to make the assessment rules suitably even—yet the per-mu tax assessed at one dan was never reduced, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy assessments were eased and light ones weighted to equalize burdens—yet the nominal per-mu rate of one dan was never actually reduced.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，御史黎貫言：「國初夏秋二稅，麥四百七十餘萬石，今少九萬；

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, Censor Li Guan said: At the beginning of the state the summer and autumn two taxes had wheat of more than four million seven hundred thousand dan; now it is ninety thousand less;
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 2 Censor Li Guan reported: "At the dynasty's founding summer and autumn taxes included more than 4.7 million dan of wheat; today we are short 90,000;

sentences.zh: 米二千四百七十餘萬石，今少二百五十餘萬。

translations.literal: rice more than twenty-four million seven hundred thousand dan; now more than two million five hundred thousand less.
translations.idiomatic: rice stood above 24.7 million dan; today we are short more than 2.5 million.

sentences.zh: 而宗室之蕃，官吏之冗，內官之眾，軍士之增，悉取給其中。

translations.literal: Yet the proliferation of the imperial clan, the redundancy of officials, the multitude of inner eunuchs, and the increase in soldiers—all draw their supply from within it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the swelling imperial clan, redundant officials, growing eunuch establishment, and expanding armies all draw on the same revenues.

sentences.zh: 賦入則日損，支費則日加。

translations.literal: Tax revenue daily diminishes while expenditures daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Revenues shrink daily while expenditures grow daily.

sentences.zh: 請核祖宗賦額及經費多寡之數，一一區畫，則知賦入有限，而浮費不容不節矣。

translations.literal: I request verification of the ancestral tax quotas and the amounts of routine expenditures, each item distinguished and planned, then one will know tax revenue is limited and inflated spending cannot but be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Audit the founding tax quotas against current spending item by item, and the court will see revenues are finite and waste cannot go unchecked.

sentences.zh: 」於是戶部議：「令天下官吏考滿遷秩，必嚴核任內租稅，徵解足數，方許給由交代。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Ministry of Revenue deliberated: Order officials throughout the realm that when their term examination for promotion is complete, they must strictly verify rent and tax within their term; only when collection and delivery reach the full quota may credentials for handover be issued.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry replied: officials seeking promotion must prove rent and tax were fully collected and remitted during their term before receiving credentials to leave office.

sentences.zh: 仍乞朝廷躬行節儉，以先天下。

translations.literal: We still beg the court personally to practice frugality, to take the lead for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We also beg the throne to practice frugality personally and lead the empire by example.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 既而諭德顧鼎臣條上錢糧積弊四事：

translations.literal: Soon after, Instructor Gu Dingchen itemized and submitted four matters of accumulated abuses in money and grain:
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Instructor Gu Dingchen submitted four reforms targeting chronic abuses in tax collection:

sentences.zh: 一曰察理田糧舊額。

translations.literal: First, investigate and put in order the old quotas for field grain.
translations.idiomatic: First, audit and regularize the original land-tax quotas.

sentences.zh: 請責州縣官，於農隙時，令裏甲等仿洪武、正統間魚鱗、風旗之式，編造圖冊，細列元額田糧、字圩、則號、條段、坍荒、成熟步口數目，官為覆勘，分別界址，履畝檢踏丈量，具開墾改正豁除之數。

translations.literal: I request holding prefectural and county officials responsible: at times between agricultural seasons, have li-jia and others follow the Hongwu and Zhengtong period fish-scale and wind-banner models to compile registers and maps, listing in detail original-quota field grain, character plots, rate numbers, strip sections, collapsed wasteland, mature field step and mouth counts; officials conduct re-survey, distinguish boundaries, walk the fields inspecting and measuring by the mu, and fully report figures for reclamation, correction, and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Hold county magistrates accountable: in slack farming seasons have li-jia compile fish-scale registers like those of Hongwu and Zhengtong, listing original quotas, plot markers, rate codes, sections, wasteland, and mature acreage; officials should resurvey boundaries, measure field by field, and report reclamation, corrections, and exemptions.

sentences.zh: 刊刻成書，收貯官庫，給散里中，永為稽考。

translations.literal: Print and bind into books, store in official treasuries, distribute in the villages, and make them the permanent standard for verification.
translations.idiomatic: Print the registers, store copies in government archives, distribute them to villages, and use them as the permanent basis for audit.

sentences.zh: 仍斟酌先年巡撫周忱、王恕簡便可行事例，立為定規。

translations.literal: Still weigh the simple feasible precedents of former grand coordinators Zhou Chen and Wang Shu and establish them as fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Adopt the workable precedents of former coordinators Zhou Chen and Wang Shu as standing rules.

sentences.zh: 取每歲實徵、起運、存留、加耗、本色、折色並處補、暫徵、帶徵、停徵等件數目，會計已定，張榜曉諭。

translations.literal: Take each year's actual collection, transport out, retention, surcharge, payment in kind, commuted payment, together with local supplements, temporary levies, attached levies, suspended levies, and other item counts; once the accounts are settled, post notices to inform the people.
translations.idiomatic: Once annual totals for actual collection, transport, reserves, surcharges, in-kind and commuted payments, supplements, temporary and attached levies are fixed, post public notices so everyone knows what is owed.

sentences.zh: 庶吏胥不得售其奸欺，而小民免賠累科擾之患。

translations.literal: Thus clerks and runners cannot sell their fraud, and common people escape the affliction of chained liability and harassing levies.
translations.idiomatic: Then clerks cannot practice fraud, and commoners will escape chained liability and harassing exactions.

sentences.zh: 一曰催徵歲辦錢糧。

translations.literal: Second, press for collection of the year's money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Second, reform the collection of annual taxes and grain.

sentences.zh: 成、弘以前，裏甲催徵，糧戶上納，糧長收解，州縣臨收。

translations.literal: Before Chenghua and Hongzhi, li-jia pressed collection, grain households delivered upward, grain chiefs received and forwarded, and prefectures and counties supervised receipt.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, li-jia pressed collection, grain households paid up, grain chiefs received and forwarded payment, and magistrates supervised receipt on the spot.

sentences.zh: 糧長不敢多收斛面，糧戶不敢攙雜水穀糠粃，兌糧官軍不敢阻難多索，公私兩便。

translations.literal: Grain chiefs dared not over-collect on the measure's surface; grain households dared not mix in water, chaff, or bran; grain-delivery soldiers dared not obstruct and demand more—public and private both benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Grain chiefs dared not pad measures, households dared not adulterate grain, and transport troops dared not obstruct delivery or demand extras—public and private interests alike were served.

sentences.zh: 近者，有司不復比較經催裏甲負糧人戶，但立限敲撲糧長，令下鄉追徵。

translations.literal: Recently, responsible officials no longer compare the li-jia who pressed collection and the grain-bearing households, but only set deadlines and beat grain chiefs, ordering them down to the villages to pursue collection.
translations.idiomatic: Lately magistrates no longer track which li-jia and households actually owe grain, but simply set deadlines, beat grain chiefs, and send them into the countryside to squeeze payment.

sentences.zh: 豪強者則大斛倍收，多方索取，所至雞犬為空。

translations.literal: The powerful then collected double with large measures and demanded from many directions, wherever they went leaving not even a chicken or dog.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful collected double with oversized measures and extorted on every pretext, leaving villages stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 孱弱者為勢豪所淩，耽延欺賴，不免變產補納。

translations.literal: The weak were bullied by powerful bullies, delayed and deceived in payment, and could not avoid selling property to make up the shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: The weak were bullied by local strongmen, delayed payment, and were forced to sell property to make up arrears.

sentences.zh: 至或舊役侵欠，責償新僉，一人逋負，株連親屬，無辜之民死於箠楚囹圄者幾數百人。

translations.literal: Some even had old appointees' embezzled arrears charged to new appointees; one person's default implicated relatives, and innocent people who died under beating and in prison numbered nearly several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Old appointees' embezzled arrears were charged to new ones; one defaulter's kin were implicated, and hundreds of innocents died under the rod or in prison.

sentences.zh: 且往時每區糧長不過正、副二名，近多至十人以上。

translations.literal: Moreover, formerly each district had no more than chief and deputy grain chiefs, two names; recently there are often more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly each district had at most a chief and deputy grain chief; now there are often more than ten.

sentences.zh: 其實收掌管糧之數少，而科斂打點使用年例之數多。

translations.literal: In fact the amount actually received and managed as grain was small, while the amount levied, marked up, used, and taken as annual precedent was large.
translations.idiomatic: In practice little grain was actually collected and accounted for, while exactions, markups, and customary fees consumed far more.

sentences.zh: 州縣一年之間，輒破中人百家之產，害莫大焉。

translations.literal: Within one year a prefecture or county would ruin the property of a hundred middling households—no harm could be greater.
translations.idiomatic: In a single year a county could ruin a hundred middling households—the harm was immense.

sentences.zh: 宜令戶部議定事例，轉行所司，審編糧長務遵舊規。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue should be ordered to deliberate precedents, transmit them to the responsible offices, and carefully appoint grain chiefs who must follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue should codify precedents, transmit them to local offices, and ensure grain chiefs are appointed strictly under the old rules.

sentences.zh: 如州縣官多僉糧長，縱容下鄉，及不委裏甲催辦，輒酷刑限比糧長者，罪之。

translations.literal: If prefectural and county officials appoint many grain chiefs, indulge them going down to villages, or do not delegate li-jia to press collection but instead use cruel torture and deadlines against grain chiefs, punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who appoint too many grain chiefs, let them run wild in the villages, or torture grain chiefs instead of using li-jia for collection should be punished.

sentences.zh: 致人命多死者，以故勘論。

translations.literal: Those causing many deaths should be investigated and prosecuted on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Those responsible for numerous deaths should be prosecuted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其二則議遣官綜理及復預備倉糧也。

translations.literal: The second and third items discussed dispatching officials for comprehensive management and restoring reserve-granary grain.
translations.idiomatic: The second and third proposals concerned dispatching officials to oversee collection and restoring reserve-granary stocks.

sentences.zh: 疏下，戶部言：「所陳俱切時弊，令所司舉行。

translations.literal: When the memorial was sent down, the Ministry of Revenue said: What was stated all hits the timely abuses; order the responsible offices to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the ministries, Revenue replied: "These proposals address urgent abuses; local offices should implement them."

sentences.zh: 」遷延數載如故。

translations.literal: " Yet delay stretched over several years and things remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet years passed and nothing changed.

sentences.zh: 糧長者，太祖時，令田多者為之，督其鄉賦稅。

translations.literal: Grain chiefs: in the Taizu's time, those with much land were made chiefs to supervise their township's rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Grain chiefs were originally wealthy landowners appointed under the Taizu to supervise local tax collection.

sentences.zh: 歲七月，州縣委官偕詣京，領勘合以行。

translations.literal: Each year in the seventh month, officials delegated by prefectures and counties accompanied them to the capital to receive verification documents before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: Each July magistrates escorted them to the capital to receive transport credentials.

sentences.zh: 糧萬石，長、副各一人，輸以時至，得召見，語合，輒蒙擢用。

translations.literal: For ten thousand dan of grain, one chief and one deputy; when delivery arrived on time they could be summoned for audience, and if their words accorded, they were often promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Districts delivering ten thousand dan had one chief and one deputy; timely delivery earned an imperial audience, and articulate chiefs were often promoted.

sentences.zh: 末年更定，每區正副二名輪充。

translations.literal: In his later years it was revised: each district had chief and deputy, two names serving in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Later the rule was fixed at two rotating appointees per district.

sentences.zh: 宣德間，復永充。

translations.literal: In the Xuande period, permanent appointment was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuande the posts again became permanent appointments.

sentences.zh: 科斂橫溢，民受其害，或私賣官糧以牟利。

translations.literal: Exactions overflowed unchecked; the people suffered harm, and some privately sold official grain for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Exactions ran wild, harming the people, and some sold official grain privately for profit.

sentences.zh: 其罷者，虧損公賦，事覺，至隕身喪家。

translations.literal: Those dismissed had damaged public revenue; when the matter came to light, they could lose their lives and ruin their families.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed chiefs who had shorted public revenue faced ruin of life and family when exposed.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，革糧長，未幾又復。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai period grain chiefs were abolished, but before long they were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingtai the post was abolished, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 自官軍兌運，糧長不復輸京師，在州里間頗滋害，故鼎臣及之。

translations.literal: Since official troops took over grain transport, grain chiefs no longer delivered to the capital but caused considerable harm within prefectures and townships—hence Dingchen addressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Once military transport replaced delivery to the capital, grain chiefs remained locally and caused great harm—hence Dingchen's critique.

sentences.zh: 未幾，御史郭弘化等亦請通行丈量，以杜包賠兼併之弊。

translations.literal: Before long Censor Guo Honghua and others also requested universal measurement to stop the abuses of blanket liability and merger.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Censor Guo Honghua and others urged empire-wide land measurement to end blanket liability and land-concealment abuses.

sentences.zh: 帝恐紛擾，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor feared disturbance and did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared disruption and refused.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐俊民言：「今之田賦，有受地於官，歲供租稅者，謂之官田。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xu Junmin said: In today's land tax, there are those who receive land from the state and yearly supply rent and tax—called official fields.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Junmin said: "Today's land tax includes official fields—land held from the state with annual rent.

sentences.zh: 有江水泛溢溝塍淹沒者，謂之坍江。

translations.literal: There are those where river water overflowed and dikes and fields were submerged—called collapsed-river fields.
translations.idiomatic: Fields submerged by river overflow are called collapsed-river land.

sentences.zh: 有流移亡絕，田棄糧存者，謂之事故。

translations.literal: There are those where people drifted away and perished, fields abandoned but grain quota remaining—called incident fields.
translations.idiomatic: Where population fled and fields lay abandoned but quotas remained are called incident wasteland.

sentences.zh: 官田貧民佃種，畝入租三斗，或五六斗或石以上者有之。

translations.literal: On official fields poor people tenant-farm; per-mu rent is three dou, or five or six dou, or more than one dan in some cases.
translations.idiomatic: Poor tenants on official land pay three dou per mu, sometimes five or six dou, sometimes more than a dan.

sentences.zh: 坍江、事故虛糧，裏甲賠納，或數十石或百餘石者有之。

translations.literal: For collapsed-river and incident phantom grain, li-jia make compensation payments—sometimes several tens of dan or more than one hundred dan.
translations.idiomatic: Li-jia must cover phantom quotas on collapsed-river and incident land—sometimes dozens or even hundreds of dan.

sentences.zh: 夫民田之價十倍官田，貧民既不能置。

translations.literal: Now civilian fields cost ten times official fields, yet poor people cannot acquire them.
translations.idiomatic: Civilian land costs ten times official land, yet the poor cannot afford even official plots.

sentences.zh: 而官田糧重，每病取盈，益以坍江、事故虛糧，又令攤納，追呼敲撲，歲無寧日。

translations.literal: Yet official-field grain is heavy, always tending toward taking the full measure; add collapsed-river and incident phantom grain with apportioned payment, pursuit, summons, and beating—year without a peaceful day.
translations.idiomatic: Official-field rates are heavy and collectors always press for the maximum; add phantom quotas and apportioned liability, with relentless pursuit and beating, and the people know no peace year-round.

sentences.zh: 而奸富猾胥方且詭寄、那移，並輕分重。

translations.literal: Meanwhile treacherous rich men and cunning clerks use false registration and shifting, merging light with heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile wealthy schemers and crafty clerks use false registration and shifting to merge light assessments with heavy ones.

sentences.zh: 此小民疾苦，閭閻凋瘁，所以日益而日增也。

translations.literal: This is the common people's affliction; lanes and wards wither—hence it daily grows.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the common people's suffering and the withering of neighborhoods—hence misery grows daily.

sentences.zh: 請定均糧、限田之制。

translations.literal: I request fixing a system of equalized grain and limited fields.
translations.idiomatic: Establish systems for equalized grain assessment and land limits.

sentences.zh: 坍江、事故，悉與蠲免。

translations.literal: Collapsed-river and incident fields, all grant exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Exempt all collapsed-river and incident phantom quotas entirely.

sentences.zh: 而合官民田為一，定上、中、下三則起科以均糧。

translations.literal: And combine official and civilian fields into one, fix upper, middle, and lower three rates for initial assessment to equalize grain.
translations.idiomatic: Merge official and civilian land into one register, assess by upper, middle, and lower rates, and equalize grain burdens.

sentences.zh: 富人不得過千畝，聽以百畝自給，其羨者則加輸邊稅。

translations.literal: The rich may not exceed one thousand mu; they are permitted one hundred mu for self-support, and the surplus pays added frontier tax.
translations.idiomatic: Cap wealthy holdings at one thousand mu, allow one hundred mu for subsistence, and levy surplus land at frontier rates.

sentences.zh: 如此，則多寡有節，輕重適宜，貧富相安，公私俱足矣。

translations.literal: Thus abundance and scarcity would have measure, light and heavy would be suitable, rich and poor would rest secure, and public and private would both be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Then scale would be regulated, burdens balanced, rich and poor at peace, and both state and people satisfied.

sentences.zh: 」部議：「疆土民俗各異，令所司熟計其便。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated: Territories and local customs differ; order the responsible offices to weigh carefully what is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry replied that customs differ by region and local offices should weigh what works.

sentences.zh: 」不行。

translations.literal: " It was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: " Nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 越數年，乃從應天巡撫侯位奏，免蘇州坍海田糧九萬餘石，然那移、飛灑之弊，相沿不改。

translations.literal: Several years later, following the memorial of Yingtian grand coordinator Hou Wei, more than ninety thousand dan of Suzhou collapsed-sea field grain was exempted, yet the abuses of shifting and scattered allocation continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, on Yingtian coordinator Hou Wei's memorial, more than 90,000 dan of Suzhou seawater-lost grain was exempted, but shifting and scattered-allocation abuses persisted.

sentences.zh: 至十八年，鼎臣為大學士，復言：「蘇、鬆、常、鎮、嘉、湖、杭七府，供輸甲天下，而裏胥豪右蠹弊特甚。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year Dingchen became Grand Secretary and again said: The seven prefectures Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou lead the realm in supply, yet li clerks and powerful elites have abuses especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, now Grand Secretary, Dingchen again reported: "The seven prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Jiaxing, Huzhou, and Hangzhou lead the empire in tax supply, yet li clerks and local elites abuse the system worst of all.

sentences.zh: 宜將欺隱及坍荒田土，一一檢核改正。

translations.literal: Concealed and collapsed wasteland fields should each be inspected, verified, and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Every concealed or wasteland holding should be audited and corrected.

sentences.zh: 」於是應天巡撫歐陽鐸檢荒田四千餘頃，計租十一萬石有奇，以所欺隱田糧六萬餘石補之，餘請豁免。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yingtian grand coordinator Ouyang Duo inspected more than four thousand qing of wasteland, reckoning rent at more than one hundred ten thousand dan; he used sixty thousand-odd dan of concealed field grain to offset it and requested exemption for the remainder.
translations.idiomatic: " Yingtian coordinator Ouyang Duo then surveyed more than 4,000 qing of wasteland worth over 110,000 dan, offset it with 60,000 dan of concealed holdings, and sought exemption for the rest.

sentences.zh: 戶部終持不下。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue ultimately held firm and would not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue still refused to approve.

sentences.zh: 時嘉興知府趙瀛建議：「田不分官、民，稅不分等則，一切以三斗起徵。

translations.literal: At that time Jiaxing prefect Zhao Ying proposed: Fields are not divided official and civilian, tax is not divided by rate grade—all are levied starting from three dou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing Prefect Zhao Ying then proposed: "Do not distinguish official and civilian land or rate grades—levy all fields from three dou per mu."

sentences.zh: 」鐸乃與蘇州知府王儀盡括官、民田裒益之。

translations.literal: " Duo then with Suzhou prefect Wang Yi fully gathered official and civilian fields and pooled increases and decreases.
translations.idiomatic: " Duo and Suzhou Prefect Wang Yi then pooled all official and civilian holdings and balanced increases against decreases.

sentences.zh: 履畝清丈，定為等則。

translations.literal: They walked the fields for clear measurement and fixed rate grades.
translations.idiomatic: They measured field by field and fixed graded rates.

sentences.zh: 所造經賦冊，以八事定稅糧：曰元額稽始，曰事故除虛，曰分項別異，曰歸總正實，曰坐派起運，曰運餘撥存，曰存餘考積，曰徵一定額。

translations.literal: The land-tax register they created used eight matters to fix tax grain: trace original quota to the beginning; remove incident phantom amounts; separate items by difference; return to total true amount; assign transport out; allocate transport surplus to retention; examine retained surplus accumulation; fix the single levy quota.
translations.idiomatic: Their land-tax register fixed grain dues in eight steps: trace original quotas; remove incident phantom amounts; itemize categories; reconcile true totals; assign transport; allocate surpluses to reserves; audit retained balances; and set the single levy quota.

sentences.zh: 又以八事考裏甲：曰丁田，曰慶賀，曰祭祀，曰鄉飲，曰科賀，曰恤政，曰公費，曰備用。

translations.literal: They also used eight matters to audit li-jia: males and fields; celebrations; sacrifices; village drinking; examination congratulations; relief administration; public expenses; and reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Li-jia accounts were audited in eight categories: population and land; celebrations; sacrifices; village feasts; examination congratulations; relief; public expenses; and reserves.

sentences.zh: 以三事定均徭：曰銀差，曰力差，曰馬差。

translations.literal: Three matters fixed equalized corvée: silver corvée, labor corvée, and horse corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Equalized corvée was set in three forms: silver, labor, and horse service.

sentences.zh: 著為例。

translations.literal: These were established as precedents.
translations.idiomatic: These rules were codified as precedent.

sentences.zh: 徵一者，總徵銀米之凡，而計畝均輸之。

translations.literal: The single levy totaled all silver and grain collections and calculated per-mu even delivery.
translations.idiomatic: The single levy pooled all silver and grain dues and spread them evenly per mu.

sentences.zh: 其科則最重與最輕者，稍以耗損益推移。

translations.literal: The heaviest and lightest rate grades were slightly shifted by gain and loss in transport surcharge.
translations.idiomatic: The heaviest and lightest assessments were slightly adjusted through transport surcharges.

sentences.zh: 重者不能盡損，惟遞減耗米，派輕齎折除之，陰予以輕。

translations.literal: The heavy could not be fully reduced; they only progressively cut transport-loss grain, assigned light transport for commuted deduction, and covertly gave relief.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy assessments could not be fully cut; transport-loss grain was reduced stepwise and light commuted deductions were assigned to ease them covertly.

sentences.zh: 輕者不能加益，為徵本色，遞增耗米加乘之，陰予以重。

translations.literal: The light could not be increased; they collected payment in kind, progressively increased transport-loss grain by multiplication, and covertly weighted them.
translations.idiomatic: Light assessments could not be openly raised; in-kind collection and multiplied transport-loss surcharges covertly increased their burden.

sentences.zh: 推收之法，以田為母，戶為子。

translations.literal: The method of pushed collection took fields as the base and households as the derivative.
translations.idiomatic: Under pushed collection, land was the base and households the derivative unit.

sentences.zh: 時豪右多梗其議，鼎臣獨以為善，曰：「是法行，吾家益千石輸，然貧民減千石矣，不可易也。

translations.literal: At the time powerful elites mostly obstructed the proposal; Dingchen alone thought it good, saying: If this law is implemented, my family will pay an added thousand dan, yet poor people will be reduced by a thousand dan—it cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful locals mostly blocked the reform, but Dingchen alone endorsed it: "If this law takes effect, my family will pay a thousand dan more, yet the poor will pay a thousand dan less—it must not be changed."

sentences.zh: 」顧其時，上不能損賦額，長民者私以己意變通。

translations.literal: " Yet at that time the throne could not reduce tax quotas, and those who governed the people privately adapted according to their own judgment.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet the throne could not cut statutory quotas, and local officials improvised as they saw fit.

sentences.zh: 由是官田不至偏重，而民田之賦反加矣。

translations.literal: Hence official fields did not become excessively heavy, but civilian-field tax instead increased.
translations.idiomatic: Official land was no longer excessively burdened, but civilian land taxes actually rose.

sentences.zh: 時又有綱銀、一串鈴諸法。

translations.literal: At the time there were also methods such as net silver and one-string-of-bells.
translations.idiomatic: Methods such as gang silver and the one-string-of-bells system also appeared.

sentences.zh: 綱銀者，舉民間應役歲費，丁四糧六總徵之，易知而不繁，猶網之有綱也。

translations.literal: Net silver: all the people's yearly corvée expenses were levied together, four-tenths by male and six-tenths by grain, easy to know and not complicated—like a net having a leading rope.
translations.idiomatic: Gang silver pooled annual corvée expenses, assessed four-tenths by household males and six-tenths by grain, simple and unified like the rope of a net.

sentences.zh: 一串鈴，則夥收分解法也。

translations.literal: One-string-of-bells was the method of collecting in bulk and dividing for distribution.
translations.idiomatic: The one-string-of-bells system collected dues in bulk and then divided them.

sentences.zh: 自是民間輸納，止收本色及折色銀矣。

translations.literal: From then on popular payment accepted only payment in kind and commuted silver.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter popular payments were accepted only in kind or commuted silver.

sentences.zh: 是時天下財賦，歲入太倉庫者二百萬兩有奇。

translations.literal: At that time empire-wide revenue entering the Grand Storehouse was more than two million taels yearly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time annual revenue to the Grand Storehouse exceeded two million taels.

sentences.zh: 舊制以七分經費而存積三分備兵、歉，以為常。

translations.literal: The old system used seven-tenths for routine expenses and retained three-tenths against troops and famine as the norm.
translations.idiomatic: The old rule spent seven-tenths on routine expenses and reserved three-tenths against war and famine.

sentences.zh: 世宗中年，邊供費繁，加以土木、禱祀，月無虛日，帑藏匱竭。

translations.literal: In the Shizong's middle years frontier supply costs were heavy; add construction and prayer sacrifices—not a month without expense—and the treasury was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizong's middle years frontier costs soared, construction and ritual spending left scarcely a month without expense, and the treasury was drained.

sentences.zh: 司農百計生財，甚至變賣寺田，收贖軍罪，猶不能給。

translations.literal: The Minister of Agriculture tried every scheme to raise revenue, even selling temple fields and collecting redemption for military offenses, yet still could not supply enough.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Revenue tried every expedient—even selling temple land and selling military pardons—yet still could not cover costs.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，俺荅犯京師，增兵設戍，餉額過倍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Altan attacked the capital region; troops were increased and garrisons set, and ration quotas more than doubled.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 Altan raided the capital region; troop increases and new garrisons more than doubled ration costs.

sentences.zh: 三十年，京邊歲用至五百九十五萬，戶部尚書孫應奎蒿目無策，乃議於南畿、浙江等州縣增賦百二十萬，加派於是始。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year capital and frontier annual expenditure reached five million nine hundred fifty thousand; Minister of Revenue Sun Yingkui looked on in dismay without strategy, and proposed increasing tax in the southern capital region, Zhejiang, and other prefectures and counties by one million two hundred thousand—supplementary levies began here.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 capital and frontier spending reached 5.95 million taels; Minister Sun Yingkui, despairing of alternatives, proposed raising taxes in the southern capital region and Zhejiang by 1.2 million taels—thus began supplementary levies.

sentences.zh: 嗣後，京邊歲用，多者過五百萬，少者亦三百餘萬，歲入不能充歲出之半。

translations.literal: Thereafter capital and frontier annual expenditure, at most exceeding five million, at least still more than three million; yearly income could not fill half of yearly outlay.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter capital and frontier spending ranged from over five million to more than three million taels, while annual income could not cover half of outlays.

sentences.zh: 由是度支為一切之法，其箕斂財賄、題增派、括贓贖、算稅契、折民壯、提編、均徭、推廣事例興焉。

translations.literal: Hence the budget office resorted to every possible method: rake collection of wealth, labeled supplementary levies, sweeping confiscations and redemptions, calculating tax deeds, converting civilian strong men, ti-bian, equalized corvée, and extending precedent purchases all arose.
translations.idiomatic: The budget office then resorted to every expedient: rake levies, labeled surcharges, confiscations and redemption sales, deed taxes, converting civilians to corvée, ti-bian, equalized corvée, and expanded precedent purchases.

sentences.zh: 其初亦賴以濟匱，久之諸所灌輸益少。

translations.literal: At first these also relied on to relieve shortage, but over time what each channel supplied grew ever less.
translations.idiomatic: At first these measures relieved shortages, but over time each source yielded less.

sentences.zh: 又四方多事，有司往往為其地奏留或請免：浙、直以備倭，川、貴以採木，山、陝、宣、大以兵荒。

translations.literal: Moreover troubles were many in the four directions; responsible offices often memorialized retention or requested exemption for their regions: Zhe and Zhi for anti-wokou, Chuan and Gui for timber cutting, Shan, Shaan, Xuan, and Da for war and famine.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile troubles multiplied everywhere and local officials sought retention or exemption: Zhejiang and Zhili for anti-pirate defense, Sichuan and Guizhou for timber, Shanxi, Shaanxi, Xuanfu, and Datong for war and famine.

sentences.zh: 不惟停格軍興所徵發，即歲額二百萬，且虧其三之一。

translations.literal: Not only were military exactions suspended, but even the annual quota of two million lost as much as one-third.
translations.idiomatic: Not only were wartime exactions suspended, but even the two-million-tael annual quota fell short by a third.

sentences.zh: 而內廷之賞給，齋殿之經營，宮中夜半出片紙，吏雖急，無敢延頃刻者。

translations.literal: Yet inner-court rewards, fasting-hall construction—when the palace issued a slip of paper at midnight, clerks though pressed dared not delay a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet inner-court rewards and ritual construction continued; a midnight slip from the palace had to be fulfilled at once, no matter how pressed the clerks were.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，大同右衛告警，賦入太倉者僅七萬，帑儲大較不及十萬。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year Datong Right Guard raised alarm; revenue entering the Grand Storehouse was only seventy thousand, and total treasury reserves fell short of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In year 37, when Datong Right Guard raised alarm, only 70,000 taels entered the Grand Storehouse and total reserves fell below 100,000.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書方鈍等憂懼不知所出，乃乘間具陳帑藏空虛狀，因條上便宜七事以請。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Fang Dun and others, anxious and fearful without knowing what to do, seized an opportunity to fully report the treasury's empty condition and itemized seven expedient measures to request.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Fang Dun and others, desperate, seized an opportunity to report the empty treasury and submit seven expedient proposals.

sentences.zh: 既，又令羣臣各條理財之策，議行者凡二十九事，益瑣屑，非國體。

translations.literal: Afterward, he also ordered the ministers each to itemize fiscal policies; twenty-nine matters were discussed for implementation, increasingly trivial and not fitting state dignity.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered ministers to submit fiscal proposals; twenty-nine were debated for implementation, most trivial and unworthy of state policy.

sentences.zh: 而累年以前積逋無不追徵，南方本色逋賦亦皆追徵折色矣。

translations.literal: Yet accumulated arrears from successive years were all pursued for collection; southern payment-in-kind arrears were also all pursued as commuted payment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet arrears from prior years were relentlessly pursued, and southern in-kind arrears were collected as commuted silver.

sentences.zh: 是時，東南被倭，南畿、浙、閩多額外提編，江南至四十萬。

translations.literal: At that time the southeast suffered wokou raids; the southern capital region, Zhe, and Min had many extra ti-bian levies, Jiangnan reaching four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast then suffered pirate raids; the southern capital region, Zhejiang, and Fujian faced extra ti-bian levies, Jiangnan alone reaching 400,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 提編者，加派之名也。

translations.literal: Ti-bian is the name for supplementary levy.
translations.idiomatic: Ti-bian was simply another name for supplementary levy.

sentences.zh: 其法，以銀力差排編十甲，如一甲不足，則提下甲補之，故謂之提編。

translations.literal: Its method: silver and labor corvée were arranged across ten jia; if one jia was insufficient, the next jia below was drawn on to supplement—hence it is called ti-bian.
translations.idiomatic: Silver and labor corvée were assessed across ten jia; if one jia fell short, the next was tapped to make up the deficit—hence ti-bian, "drawing on the next jia."

sentences.zh: 及倭患平，應天巡撫周如鬥乞減加派，給事中何煃亦具陳南畿困敝，言：「軍門養兵，工部料價，操江募兵，兵備道壯丁，府州縣鄉兵，率為民累，甚者指一科十，請禁革之。

translations.literal: When the wokou threat subsided, Yingtian grand coordinator Zhou Rudou begged reduction of supplementary levies; Supervising Secretary He Kun also fully reported the southern capital region's exhaustion, saying: Military headquarters maintaining troops, Works Ministry material prices, Yangzi defense recruiting soldiers, defense circuit strong youths, prefectural and county militia—all became burdens on the people; in extreme cases one category became ten. I request prohibition and abolition.
translations.idiomatic: After the pirate threat eased, Yingtian coordinator Zhou Rudou sought cuts to supplementary levies; Supervising Secretary He Kun reported the southern capital region's exhaustion: "Troop maintenance, Works Ministry materials, Yangzi defense recruitment, circuit militia, and county levies all burden the people—sometimes one category becomes ten. Abolish these abuses."

sentences.zh: 」命如煃議，而提編之額不能減。

translations.literal: " He ordered according to He Kun's proposal, yet the ti-bian quota could not be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: " The court followed He's proposal in principle, but ti-bian quotas could not be cut.

sentences.zh: 隆、萬之世，增額既如故，又多無藝之徵，逋糧愈多，規避亦益巧。

translations.literal: In the Longqing and Wanli reigns, increased quotas remained as before, and there were also many levies without proper category; grain arrears grew ever more, and evasion grew ever more artful.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longqing and Wanli, supplementary quotas persisted, irregular exactions multiplied, arrears mounted, and evasion grew ever more sophisticated.

sentences.zh: 已解而愆限或至十餘年，未徵而報收，一縣有至十萬者。

translations.literal: Already delivered yet overdue in deadline for as much as more than ten years; not yet collected yet reported as received—one county could reach one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Delivered grain could remain overdue for more than ten years; uncollected dues were reported as received—single counties showed false receipts of 100,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 逋欠之多，縣各數十萬。

translations.literal: Arrears were so great that each county had several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears ran to hundreds of thousands per county.

sentences.zh: 賴行一條鞭法，無他科擾，民力不大絀。

translations.literal: Fortunately the single-whip method was implemented, without other categories harassing them, and the people's strength was not greatly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately the single-whip law was enforced, other exactions were curbed, and popular strength was not utterly broken.

sentences.zh: 一條鞭法者，總括一州縣之賦役，量地計丁，丁糧畢輸於官。

translations.literal: The single-whip method: it summarized a prefecture or county's taxes and corvée, measured land and calculated males, and males' grain was all delivered to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The single-whip law pooled a prefecture or county's taxes and corvée, assessed land and household males, and required all grain and labor dues to be paid to the state.

sentences.zh: 一歲之役，官為僉募。

translations.literal: A year's corvée was recruited by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Annual corvée was hired by the government.

sentences.zh: 力差，則計其工食之費，量為增減；

translations.literal: For labor corvée, the cost of work and food was calculated and increased or decreased as appropriate;
translations.idiomatic: Labor corvée was commuted by calculating wages and rations, adjusted up or down as needed;

sentences.zh: 銀差，則計其交納之費，加以增耗。

translations.literal: for silver corvée, the cost of delivery was calculated and transport surcharge added.
translations.idiomatic: silver corvée by calculating delivery costs plus transport surcharges.

sentences.zh: 凡額辦、派辦、京庫歲需與存留、供億諸費，以及土貢方物，悉並為一條，皆計畝徵銀，折辦於官，故謂之一條鞭。

translations.literal: All quota assignments, dispatched assignments, capital-storehouse annual needs, retention, supply expenses, and local tribute goods were all merged into one item, all levied in silver per mu and commuted for the state—hence it is called one whip.
translations.idiomatic: Quota assignments, dispatched duties, capital needs, local reserves, supply costs, and tribute goods were merged into one levy, assessed per mu in silver and remitted to officials—hence the single whip.

sentences.zh: 立法頗為簡便。

translations.literal: The legislation was quite simple and convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The law was notably simpler to administer.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間，數行數止，至萬曆九年乃盡行之。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing period it was implemented and halted several times; only in the ninth year of Wanli was it fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing it was tried and suspended repeatedly; full empire-wide implementation came only in Wanli year 9.

sentences.zh: 其後接踵三大徵，頗有加派，事畢旋已。

translations.literal: Afterward three great levies followed in succession, with considerable supplementary assignments; when each affair ended they were soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Three major wartime surcharges followed in succession, each lifted when the crisis ended.

sentences.zh: 至四十六年，驟增遼餉三百萬。

translations.literal: By the forty-sixth year Liaodong rations were suddenly increased by three million.
translations.idiomatic: In year 46 Liaodong military funds were suddenly raised by three million taels.

sentences.zh: 時內帑充積，帝靳不肯發。

translations.literal: At the time the inner treasury was full and accumulated, but the emperor was stingy and unwilling to disburse.
translations.idiomatic: The inner treasury was full, yet the emperor refused to release funds.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書李汝華乃援徵倭、播例，畝加三釐五毫，天下之賦增二百萬有奇。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Li Ruhua then cited the precedents of anti-wokou and Bozhou campaigns, adding three li five hao per mu; empire-wide tax increased by more than two million.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Ruhua cited anti-pirate and Bozhou precedents and added 3.5 li per mu, raising empire-wide taxes by more than two million taels.

sentences.zh: 明年復加三釐五毫。

translations.literal: The next year another three li five hao was added.
translations.idiomatic: The following year another 3.5 li per mu was added.

sentences.zh: 明年，以兵工二部請，復加二釐。

translations.literal: The next year, at the request of the Ministries of War and Works, another two li was added.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, at the request of War and Works, another 2 li was added.

sentences.zh: 通前後九釐，增賦五百二十萬，遂為歲額。

translations.literal: Altogether nine li before and after, tax increased by five million two hundred thousand, and this became the annual quota.
translations.idiomatic: The nine li combined raised taxes by 5.2 million taels, which became the new annual quota.

sentences.zh: 所不加者，畿內八府及貴州而已。

translations.literal: Those not subject to increase were only the eight prefectures within the capital region and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only the eight capital-region prefectures and Guizhou were exempt.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，給事中甄淑言：「遼餉加派，易致不均。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, Supervising Secretary Zhen Shu said: Supplementary Liaodong rations easily lead to inequality.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year 1 Supervising Secretary Zhen Shu said: "Supplementary Liaodong levies easily produce unfair distribution.

sentences.zh: 蓋天下戶口有戶口之銀，人丁有人丁之銀，田土有田土之銀，有司徵收，總曰銀額。

translations.literal: For throughout the realm households have household silver, persons have person silver, fields have field silver; when responsible offices collect, the total is called the silver quota.
translations.idiomatic: Households, males, and land each carry their own silver assessments; officials collect them into a total silver quota.

sentences.zh: 按銀加派，則其數不漏。

translations.literal: If supplementary levy follows the silver quota, the amount will not leak.
translations.idiomatic: Assessing surcharges against the silver quota ensures nothing is missed.

sentences.zh: 東西南北之民，甘苦不同，布帛粟米力役之法，徵納不同。

translations.literal: The people of east, west, south, and north differ in hardship and ease; methods for cloth, silk, grain, and labor corvée and their collection differ.
translations.idiomatic: People across the realm differ in hardship; cloth, grain, and labor dues are collected differently by region.

sentences.zh: 惟守令自知其甘苦，而通融其徵納。

translations.literal: Only magistrates know their hardship and ease themselves and adapt collection flexibly.
translations.idiomatic: Only local magistrates know local conditions and can adjust collection flexibly.

sentences.zh: 今因人土之宜，則無偏枯之累。

translations.literal: Now if one follows the suitability of people and land, there will be no burden of one-sided hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Following local conditions avoids one-sided hardship.

sentences.zh: 其法，以銀額為主，而通人情，酌土俗，頒示直省。

translations.literal: Its method takes the silver quota as primary, accommodates human circumstances, weighs local custom, and is promulgated to the directly governed provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The method takes the silver quota as its base, accommodates local custom, and is promulgated to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 每歲存留、起解各項銀兩之數，以所加餉額，按銀數分派，總提折扣，裒多益寡，期不失餉額而止。

translations.literal: Each year's retained and forwarded silver amounts, using the added ration quota, are distributed by silver count, totaled and discounted, pooling abundance to aid scarcity, aiming only not to fall short of the ration quota.
translations.idiomatic: Annual retained and forwarded silver is apportioned by silver quota against the added military funds, pooled and discounted from rich to poor districts, without falling short of the ration total.

sentences.zh: 如此，則愚民易知，可杜奸胥意為增減之弊。

translations.literal: Thus simple people easily understand, and the abuse of clerks deliberately increasing or decreasing can be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners would understand easily, and clerks could no longer manipulate assessments at will.

sentences.zh: 且小民所最苦者，無田之糧，無米之丁，田鬻富室，產去糧存，而猶輸丁賦。

translations.literal: Moreover what common people suffer most is grain tax without fields, male tax without grain: fields sold to wealthy households, property gone but grain quota remains, yet they still pay male tax.
translations.idiomatic: Worst of all is grain tax without land and male tax without grain: when land is sold to the rich, the quota remains but the seller still owes male tax.

sentences.zh: 宜取額丁、額米，兩衡而定其數，米若干即帶丁若干。

translations.literal: One should take quota males and quota grain, balance both to fix the number: so much grain carries so many males.
translations.idiomatic: Balance quota grain and quota males so that a given grain assessment carries a fixed number of males.

sentences.zh: 買田者，收米便收丁，則縣冊不失丁額，貧民不致賠累，而有司亦免逋賦之患。
