translations.literal: When one buys fields, collecting grain collects males too; then the county register does not lose male quota, poor people avoid chained liability, and responsible offices also escape arrears in tax.
translations.idiomatic: When land is sold, grain and male quotas transfer together; county registers stay accurate, the poor avoid chained liability, and magistrates escape arrears.

sentences.zh: 」下部覆議，從之。

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated in reply and followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry approved and implemented the proposal.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，軍興，兵部尚書樑廷棟請增田賦。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen, with war begun, Minister of War Liang Tingdong requested increase of land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 3, as war resumed, Minister of War Liang Tingdong sought a land-tax increase.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書畢自嚴不能止，乃於九釐外畝復徵三釐。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Bi Ziyan could not stop it and levied another three li per mu beyond the nine li.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Bi Ziyan could not stop it and added another 3 li per mu atop the existing 9 li.

sentences.zh: 惟順天、永平以新被兵無所加，餘六府畝徵六釐，得他省之半，共增賦百六十五萬四千有奇。

translations.literal: Only Shuntian and Yongping, newly afflicted by troops, had no increase; the other six prefectures levied six li per mu, half that of other provinces, totaling an added tax of more than one million six hundred fifty-four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shuntian and Yongping, recently ravaged by war, were exempt; the other six prefectures paid 6 li per mu—half the provincial rate—raising taxes by more than 1.654 million taels.

sentences.zh: 後五年，總督盧象升請加宦戶田賦十之一，民糧十兩以上同之。

translations.literal: Five years later Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng requested adding one-tenth to official-household land tax, and the same for civilian grain tax above ten taels.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later Grand Coordinator Lu Xiangsheng proposed a ten-percent surcharge on official-household land tax and on civilian taxes above ten taels.

sentences.zh: 既而概徵每兩一錢，名曰助餉。

translations.literal: Soon after a general levy of one cash per tael was imposed, called aid-rations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a flat levy of one cash per tael was imposed, called aid-rations.

sentences.zh: 越二年，復行均輸法，因糧輸餉，畝計米六合，石折銀八錢，又畝加徵一分四釐九絲。

translations.literal: Two years later the equalized transport method was restored: grain paid rations, six he per mu calculated, one dan converted to eight qian silver, and per mu another levy of one fen four li nine si.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later equalized transport was restored: grain paid military funds at six he per mu, one dan commuted to eight qian silver, plus another 1.49 fen per mu.

sentences.zh: 越二年，楊嗣昌督師，畝加練餉銀一分。

translations.literal: Two years later Yang Sichang supervised the army and added training-ration silver of one fen per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, under Yang Sichang's command, training-ration silver of one fen per mu was added.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎張若麒請收兵殘遺產為官莊，分上、中、下，畝納租八斗至二三斗有差。

translations.literal: War Ministry secretary Zhang Ruoqi requested collecting abandoned property from military devastation as official estates, divided upper, middle, and lower, with rent from eight dou down to two or three dou per mu varying.
translations.idiomatic: War Ministry secretary Zhang Ruoqi proposed seizing war-abandoned land as official estates graded upper, middle, and lower, with rent from eight to two or three dou per mu.

sentences.zh: 御史衛周胤言：「嗣昌流毒天下，剿練之餉多至七百萬，民怨何極。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Zhouyin said: Yang Sichang's poison spreads through the realm; suppression-and-training rations reach as much as seven million—how extreme is popular resentment?
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Zhouyin said: "Yang Sichang's policies poison the realm; suppression and training funds exceed seven million—popular resentment knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 」御史郝晉亦言：「萬曆末年，合九邊餉止二百八十萬。

translations.literal: " Censor Hao Jin also said: At the end of Wanli, combined nine-frontier rations were only two million eight hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor Hao Jin added: "At the end of Wanli the nine frontiers together received only 2.8 million taels.

sentences.zh: 今加派遼餉至九百萬。

translations.literal: Now supplementary Liaodong rations reach nine million.
translations.idiomatic: Now supplementary Liaodong funds reach nine million.

sentences.zh: 剿餉三百三十萬，業已停罷，旋加練餉七百三十餘萬。

translations.literal: Suppression rations of three million three hundred thousand had already been halted, then training rations of more than seven million three hundred thousand were added.
translations.idiomatic: Suppression funds of 3.3 million had been suspended, then training funds of more than 7.3 million were added.

sentences.zh: 自古有一年而括二千萬以輸京師，又括京師二千萬以輸邊者乎？

translations.literal: Since antiquity has there ever been one year in which twenty million was raked in for the capital, then twenty million from the capital raked in for the frontier?
translations.idiomatic: When in history was twenty million raked in for the capital in one year, then another twenty million from the capital sent to the frontier?

sentences.zh: 」疏語雖切直，而時事危急，不能從也。

translations.literal: " Though the memorial's words were blunt and direct, the times were critically urgent and it could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: " Though blunt, the memorial could not be heeded in a crisis.

sentences.zh: 役法定於洪武元年。

translations.literal: Corvée law was fixed in the first year of Hongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée law was codified in Hongwu year 1.

sentences.zh: 田一頃出丁夫一人，不及頃者以他田足之，名曰均工夫。

translations.literal: One qing of fields produced one adult male laborer; where less than a qing, other fields made it up—called equalized labor.
translations.idiomatic: One qing of land owed one adult laborer; smaller holdings were grouped to meet the quota—called equalized labor.

sentences.zh: 尋編應天十八府州，江西九江、饒州、南康三府均工夫圖冊。

translations.literal: Soon registers and maps of equalized labor were compiled for Yingtian's eighteen prefectures and subprefectures and Jiangxi's Jiujiang, Raozhou, and Nankang three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Registers of equalized labor were soon compiled for Yingtian's eighteen prefectures and for Jiujiang, Raozhou, and Nankang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 每歲農隙赴京，供役三十日遣歸。

translations.literal: Each year in the farming slack season they went to the capital, served thirty days, and were sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Each year in the farming slack season they served thirty days in the capital and returned home.

sentences.zh: 田多丁少者，以佃人充夫，而田主出米一石資其用。

translations.literal: Where fields were many but males few, tenants served as laborers while the landowner provided one dan of grain for their expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Where land exceeded available males, tenants served as laborers while landowners paid one dan of grain for their support.

sentences.zh: 非佃人而計畝出夫者，畝資米二升五合。

translations.literal: Where not tenants but per-mu labor was supplied, each mu provided two sheng five he of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Where labor was hired by the mu rather than through tenants, each mu paid two sheng five he of grain.

sentences.zh: 迨造黃冊成，以一百十戶為一里，裏分十甲曰裏甲。

translations.literal: When the yellow registers were completed, one hundred ten households formed one li; the li was divided into ten jia called li-jia.
translations.idiomatic: When the yellow registers were completed, 110 households formed one li, subdivided into ten jia as li-jia units.

sentences.zh: 以上、中、下戶為三等，五歲均役，十歲一更造。

translations.literal: Upper, middle, and lower households formed three grades; corvée was equalized every five years and registers renewed every ten.
translations.idiomatic: Households ranked upper, middle, or lower; corvée rotated every five years and registers were renewed every ten.

sentences.zh: 一歲中諸歲雜目應役者，編第均之，銀、力從所便，曰均徭。

translations.literal: Within one year all miscellaneous annual items requiring service were arranged in sequence and equalized; silver or labor as convenient—called equalized corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Annual miscellaneous duties were sequenced and equalized, payable in silver or labor as convenient—equalized corvée.

sentences.zh: 他雜役。

translations.literal: Other miscellaneous corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Other miscellaneous corvée duties followed.

sentences.zh: 凡祗應、禁子、弓兵，悉僉市民，毋役糧戶。

translations.literal: All attendants, runners, and bow soldiers were recruited from townspeople, not from grain households.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants, runners, and bow troops were recruited from townspeople, not grain-tax households.

sentences.zh: 額外科一錢、役一夫者，罪流徙。

translations.literal: Anyone levying one cash beyond quota or one laborer beyond quota was punished with exile.
translations.idiomatic: Extra levies of even one cash or one laborer beyond quota were punishable by exile.

sentences.zh: 後法稍馳，編徭役裏甲者，以戶為斷，放大戶而勾單小。

translations.literal: Later the law slackened somewhat; those compiling corvée and li-jia took households as the unit, favoring large households and pressing small ones.
translations.idiomatic: Later enforcement slackened: corvée compilers favored large households and squeezed small ones.

sentences.zh: 於是議者言，均徭之法，按冊籍丁糧，以資產為宗，核人戶上下，以蓄藏得實也。

translations.literal: Thereupon debaters said: The equalized corvée method, following register males and grain with assets as principle, or verifying household rank with stored wealth as reality.
translations.idiomatic: Critics noted two approaches to equalized corvée: assess by registered males and grain with wealth as the standard, or rank households by stored assets.

sentences.zh: 稽冊籍，則富商大賈免役，而土著困；

translations.literal: Checking registers, great merchants escaped corvée while natives were distressed;
translations.idiomatic: Following registers let wealthy merchants escape corvée while natives suffered;

sentences.zh: 核人戶，則官吏裏胥輕重其手，而小民益窮蹙。

translations.literal: verifying households, officials and li clerks weighted their hands, and common people grew ever more impoverished.
translations.idiomatic: ranking households let officials and li clerks manipulate assessments, crushing commoners further.

sentences.zh: 二者交病。

translations.literal: Both methods were mutually afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Both approaches failed.

sentences.zh: 然專論丁糧，庶幾古人租庸調之意。

translations.literal: Yet focusing solely on males and grain might approximate the ancient meaning of zu, yong, and diao.
translations.idiomatic: Focusing solely on males and grain might approximate the Tang zu-yong-diao system.

sentences.zh: 乃令以舊編力差、銀差之數當丁糧之數，難易輕重酌其中。

translations.literal: They then ordered using old compiled labor-corvée and silver-corvée counts in place of male-and-grain counts, weighing difficulty, ease, light, and heavy within.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then substituted old labor and silver corvée totals for male-and-grain counts, balancing light and heavy burdens.

sentences.zh: 役以應差，裏甲除當復者，論丁糧多少編次先後，曰鼠尾冊，按而徵之。

translations.literal: Corvée followed due rotation; li-jia except those due for rest were ordered by male-and-grain amount in sequence first to last—called the rat-tail register—and levied accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée rotated by due turn; li-jia not on rest leave were sequenced by male-and-grain burden in the rat-tail register and levied in order.

sentences.zh: 市民商賈家殷足而無田產者，聽自佔，以佐銀差。

translations.literal: Townsmen and merchants whose families were wealthy but without land were permitted self-registration to assist silver corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy townsmen and merchants without land could register voluntarily to help meet silver corvée quotas.

sentences.zh: 正統初，僉事夏時創行於江西，他省仿行之，役以稍平。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengtong, Commissioner Xia Shi pioneered it in Jiangxi; other provinces imitated it, and corvée became somewhat even.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengtong Commissioner Xia Shi pioneered the reform in Jiangxi; other provinces followed, and corvée burdens eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 其後諸上供者，官為支解，而官府公私所須，復給所輸銀於坊裏長，責其營辦。

translations.literal: Afterward all items for court supply were disbursed by officials, but what government offices needed publicly and privately was again given from submitted silver to ward and li chiefs, charging them to arrange provision.
translations.idiomatic: Later court supplies were disbursed by officials, but local government needs were again funded from submitted silver given to ward and li chiefs to arrange.

sentences.zh: 給不能一二，供者或什伯，甚至無所給，惟計值年裏甲祗應夫馬飲食，而裏甲病矣。

translations.literal: What was given did not reach one or two tenths; what was required might be tenfold or hundredfold, even nothing given at all—only reckoning the annual value of li-jia attendants', runners', horses', and food, and li-jia were afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: They received perhaps one or two tenths of what was required, sometimes ten or a hundred times as much, sometimes nothing—li-jia were charged the full cost of attendants, runners, horses, and food, and were ruined.

sentences.zh: 凡均徭，解戶上供為京徭，主納為中官留難，不易中納，往復改貿，率至傾產。

translations.literal: For equalized corvée, forwarding households supplying the capital was capital corvée; chief deliverers were obstructed by inner eunuchs, middle delivery was not easy, back-and-forth commodity changes usually ended in ruined property.
translations.idiomatic: Under equalized corvée, forwarding households supplying the capital faced capital corvée; chief deliverers were obstructed by eunuchs, commuted payment was difficult, and repeated commodity exchanges usually ruined families.

sentences.zh: 其他役苛索之弊，不可毛舉。

translations.literal: Other abuses of harsh exaction in corvée cannot be counted one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Other corvée abuses of harsh exaction are too numerous to list.

sentences.zh: 明初，令天下貢土所有，有常額，珍奇玩好不與。

translations.literal: Early in the Ming, the realm was ordered to tribute local products with fixed quotas; rare curios and playthings were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming orders fixed local tribute quotas and excluded rare curios and luxuries.

sentences.zh: 即須用，編之裏甲，出銀以市。

translations.literal: When needed, it was assigned to li-jia, who paid silver to purchase on the market.
translations.idiomatic: When items were needed, li-jia were assigned to buy them with silver on the market.

sentences.zh: 顧其目冗碎，奸黠者緣為利孔。

translations.literal: Yet the items were numerous and fragmented, and the cunning used them as profit holes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the categories were fragmented, giving the cunning room for profit.

sentences.zh: 又大工營繕，祠官祝釐，資用繁溢。

translations.literal: Moreover great works of construction and repair, shrine officials' prayer blessings—expenditures overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Major construction and shrine rituals multiplied expenditures without end.

sentences.zh: 迨至中葉，倭寇交訌，仍歲河決，國用耗殫。

translations.literal: By the middle period wokou raids intertwined, rivers burst year after year, and state expenditures were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-dynasty pirate raids and annual river floods exhausted state finances.

sentences.zh: 於是裏甲、均徭，浮於歲額矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon li-jia and equalized corvée floated above the annual quota.
translations.idiomatic: Li-jia and equalized corvée then exceeded annual quotas.

sentences.zh: 凡役民，自裏甲正辦外，如糧長、解戶、馬船頭、館夫、祗候、弓兵、皁隸、門禁、廚鬥為常役。

translations.literal: All corvée on the people, apart from li-jia regular duties, such as grain chiefs, forwarding households, horse-boat heads, inn attendants, runners, bow soldiers, black-clad runners, gate guards, and kitchen stewards were standing corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond regular li-jia duties, standing corvée included grain chiefs, forwarding households, boat heads, inn attendants, runners, bow troops, runners in black, gate guards, and kitchen stewards.

sentences.zh: 後又有斫薪、擡柴、修河、修倉、運料、接遞、站鋪、插淺夫之類，因事編僉，歲有增益。

translations.literal: Later there were also wood-cutting, firewood-carrying, river repair, granary repair, material transport, relay delivery, courier stations, and shallow-water laborers—compiled and recruited as affairs arose, increasing yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Later came woodcutting, firewood hauling, river and granary repair, material transport, relay service, courier stations, and shallow-water labor—recruited as needs arose and increasing yearly.

sentences.zh: 嘉、隆後，行一條鞭法，通計一省丁糧，均派一省徭役。

translations.literal: After Jiajing and Longqing, the single-whip method was implemented: totaling one province's males and grain, evenly assigning one province's corvée.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiajing and Longqing the single-whip law totaled each province's males and grain and spread corvée evenly province-wide.

sentences.zh: 於是均徭、裏甲與兩稅為一，小民得無擾，而事亦易集。

translations.literal: Thereupon equalized corvée, li-jia, and the two taxes became one; common people were not harassed, and affairs were also easy to gather.
translations.idiomatic: Equalized corvée, li-jia, and the two taxes merged; commoners were less harassed and collection was easier.

sentences.zh: 然糧長、裏長，名罷實存，諸役卒至，復僉農氓。

translations.literal: Yet grain chiefs and li chiefs, abolished in name but existing in fact—when corvée duties arrived, peasants were again recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Yet grain chiefs and li chiefs survived in practice; when duties arose, peasants were conscripted again.

sentences.zh: 條鞭法行十餘年，規制頓紊，不能盡遵也。

translations.literal: After the whip method had been in force more than ten years, regulations suddenly fell into disorder and could not be fully followed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years the single-whip regulations fell into disorder and were no longer fully observed.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，御史李應升疏陳十害，其三條切言馬夫、河役、糧甲、修辦、白役擾民之弊。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period Censor Li Yingsheng memorialized ten harms; three items bluntly addressed the abuses of horse grooms, river corvée, grain jia, repair provisions, and white corvée harassing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi Censor Li Yingsheng listed ten abuses; three addressed horse grooms, river corvée, grain jia, repair duties, and unauthorized white corvée harassing the people.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年，河南巡撫範景文言：「民所患苦，莫如差役。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen Henan grand coordinator Fan Jingwen said: What the people suffer most is none other than dispatched corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year 3 Henan coordinator Fan Jingwen said: "Nothing afflicts the people like dispatched corvée.

sentences.zh: 錢糧有收戶、解戶、驛遞有馬戶，供應有行戶，皆僉有力之家充之，名曰大戶。

translations.literal: For money and grain there were collecting households and forwarding households; for courier relay there were horse households; for supply there were broker households—all recruited from powerful families, called great households.
translations.idiomatic: Money and grain had collecting and forwarding households; courier relay had horse households; supplies had broker households—all recruited from powerful families called great households.

sentences.zh: 究之，所僉非富民，中人之產輒為之傾。

translations.literal: Investigating it, those recruited were not wealthy households; middling property was often ruined by it.
translations.idiomatic: In practice those recruited were not the truly wealthy; middling households were often ruined.

sentences.zh: 自變為條鞭法，以境內之役均於境內之糧，宜少蘇矣，乃民間仍歲奔走，罄資津貼，是條鞭行而大戶未嘗革也。

translations.literal: Since changing to the whip method, spreading duties within the territory evenly across grain within the territory, there should have been slight relief—yet the people still ran about yearly, exhausting funds for subsidies: the whip was implemented but great households were never reformed.
translations.idiomatic: The single-whip law spread duties across local grain and should have eased burdens, yet people still ran themselves ragged yearly paying subsidies—the whip was enforced but great-household abuses were never abolished.

sentences.zh: 」時給事中劉懋復奏裁驛夫，徵調往來，仍責編戶。

translations.literal: " At the time Supervising Secretary Liu Mao again memorialized to cut courier laborers; requisitions and transfers back and forth still charged registered households.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising Secretary Liu Mao then memorialized to cut courier staff, but requisitions still fell on registered households.

sentences.zh: 驛夫無所得食，至相率從流賊為亂云。

translations.literal: Courier laborers had no food to obtain, until they banded together to follow bandits in rebellion, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Courier laborers went unfed until, it is said, they joined bandits in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 凡軍、匠、竈戶，役皆永充。

translations.literal: All military, artisan, and salt-maker households served corvée in permanent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Military, artisan, and salt-maker households all served hereditary corvée.

sentences.zh: 軍戶死若逃者，於原籍勾補。

translations.literal: When military households died or fled, they were traced and supplemented from original registers.
translations.idiomatic: When military households lost members through death or flight, replacements were traced from original registers.

sentences.zh: 匠戶二等：曰住坐，曰輪班。

translations.literal: Artisan households were two grades: called resident and rotating shift.
translations.idiomatic: Artisan households fell into two grades: resident and rotating shift.

sentences.zh: 住坐之匠，月上工十日。

translations.literal: Resident artisans worked ten days per month.
translations.idiomatic: Resident artisans worked ten days a month.

sentences.zh: 不赴班者，輸罰班銀月六錢，故謂之輸班。

translations.literal: Those not attending shift paid penalty-shift silver of six qian monthly—hence called paying shift.
translations.idiomatic: Those who skipped shifts paid six qian monthly in lieu—called shift payment.

sentences.zh: 監局中官，多佔匠役，又括充幼匠，動以千計，死若逃者，勾補如軍。

translations.literal: Eunuchs in supervisory bureaus often seized artisan corvée, also swept up juvenile artisans by the thousands; when they died or fled, tracing and supplement followed military households.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs in supervisory bureaus seized artisans, conscripted juveniles by the thousands, and traced replacements as with military households when they died or fled.

sentences.zh: 竈戶有上、中、下三等。

translations.literal: Salt-maker households had upper, middle, and lower three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-maker households ranked upper, middle, or lower.

sentences.zh: 每一正丁，貼以餘丁。

translations.literal: Each principal male was supplemented with surplus males.
translations.idiomatic: Each principal male was supplemented by additional males.

sentences.zh: 上、中戶丁力多，或貼二三丁，下戶概予優免。

translations.literal: Upper and middle households had many males and strength, sometimes supplemented by two or three males; lower households were generally given preferential exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Upper and middle households with many males might attach two or three supplements; lower households were generally exempted.

sentences.zh: 他如陵戶、園戶、海戶、廟戶、幡夫、庫役，瑣末不可勝計。

translations.literal: Others such as tomb households, garden households, sea households, temple households, banner bearers, and treasury laborers—trivial items too numerous to count.
translations.idiomatic: Others—tomb, garden, sea, and temple households, banner bearers, treasury laborers—were too numerous to list.

sentences.zh: 明初，工役之繁，自營建兩京宗廟、宮殿、闕門、王邸，採木、陶甓，工匠造作，以萬萬計。

translations.literal: Early Ming labor corvée was so heavy—from constructing the two capitals' ancestral temples, palaces, gate towers, and princely mansions, timber cutting, pottery and brick, artisan manufacture—counted by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming labor corvée was immense: building capitals, temples, palaces, gates, and princely mansions, cutting timber, making bricks and tiles, and employing artisans by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 所在築城、浚陂，百役具舉。

translations.literal: Everywhere city building and moat dredging—a hundred corvées all raised.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere cities were built and moats dredged—a hundred kinds of corvée at once.

sentences.zh: 迄於洪、宣，郊壇、倉庾猶未迄工。

translations.literal: Down to Hongwu and Xuande, suburban altars and granaries were still not finished.
translations.idiomatic: Through Hongwu and Xuande suburban altars and granaries were still unfinished.

sentences.zh: 正統、天順之際，三殿、兩宮、南內、離宮，次第興建。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong and Tianshun period, the three halls, two palaces, southern inner quarters, and detached palaces were built in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengtong and Tianshun the three main halls, two palaces, southern inner quarters, and detached palaces were built one after another.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，大學士劉吉言：「近年工役，俱摘發京營軍士，內外軍官禁不得估工用大小多寡。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi period Grand Secretary Liu Ji said: In recent years labor corvée all drew on capital-garrison soldiers; inner and outer military officers were forbidden from estimating the size and amount of work used.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi Grand Secretary Liu Ji said: "Recent projects all conscript capital-garrison troops, while officers are barred from controlling how much labor is actually used.

sentences.zh: 本用五千人，奏請至一二萬，無所稽覈。

translations.literal: Originally five thousand men were needed, but memorials requested ten or twenty thousand, with nothing to audit.
translations.idiomatic: Projects needing five thousand men were reported as requiring ten or twenty thousand, with no audit.

sentences.zh: 」禮部尚書倪嶽言：「諸役費動以數十萬計，水旱相仍，乞少停止。

translations.literal: " Minister of Rites Ni Yue said: All corvée costs often run to several hundred thousand; flood and drought follow in succession—I beg that some be halted.
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Rites Ni Yue added: "Corvée costs routinely reach hundreds of thousands; floods and droughts persist—please suspend some projects.

sentences.zh: 」南京禮部尚書童軒復陳工役之苦。

translations.literal: " Nanjing Minister of Rites Tong Xuan again reported the suffering of labor corvée.
translations.idiomatic: " Nanjing Minister of Rites Tong Xuan again described the suffering caused by labor corvée.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書林瀚亦言：「兩畿頻年兇災，困於百役，窮愁怨歎。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Lin Han also said: The two capital regions have suffered famine year after year, distressed by a hundred corvées, poor, anxious, resentful, and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Lin Han also said: "The two capital regions suffer famine year after year, crushed by countless corvées, sunk in poverty, resentment, and despair.

sentences.zh: 山、陝供億軍興，雲南、廣東西徵發剿叛。

translations.literal: Shan and Shaan supply military campaigns; Yunnan and Guangdong and Guangxi mobilize for suppressing rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi and Shaanxi feed military campaigns; Yunnan, Guangdong, and Guangxi mobilize against rebels.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南、湖廣、四川、江西興造王邸，財力不贍。

translations.literal: Shandong, Henan, Huguang, Sichuan, and Jiangxi build princely mansions—financial strength cannot cover it.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong, Henan, Huguang, Sichuan, and Jiangxi build princely mansions beyond their means.

sentences.zh: 浙江、福建辦物料，視舊日增多。

translations.literal: Zhejiang and Fujian supply materials, increased compared with former days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang and Fujian supply materials in greater amounts than before.

sentences.zh: 庫藏空匱，不可不慮。

translations.literal: Treasury stores are empty and depleted—this cannot but be considered.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury stores are empty—this cannot be ignored.

sentences.zh: 」帝皆納其言，然不能盡從也。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted all their words, yet could not fully follow them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted their advice but could not follow it fully.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，乾清宮役尤大。

translations.literal: In the Wuzong period labor on the Palace of Heavenly Purity was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong work on the Palace of Heavenly Purity was especially heavy.

sentences.zh: 乙太素殿初制樸儉，改作雕峻，用銀至二千萬餘兩，役工匠三千餘人，歲支工食米萬三千餘石。

translations.literal: The Hall of Great Simplicity was first built plain and frugal, then changed to carved grandeur, using more than twenty million taels of silver, employing more than three thousand artisans, with annual worker grain rations of more than thirteen thousand dan.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Great Simplicity, first built plainly, was rebuilt in ornate style at a cost of more than twenty million taels, employing over three thousand artisans and thirteen thousand dan of grain rations yearly.

sentences.zh: 又修凝翠、昭和、崇智、光霽諸殿，御馬臨、鐘鼓司、南城豹房新房、火藥庫皆鼎新之。

translations.literal: They also repaired the halls Ningcui, Zhaohe, Chongzhi, and Guangji; the Imperial Horse Stables, Bell and Drum Office, new buildings at the southern-city Leopard Quarters, and the gunpowder storehouse—all were made new.
translations.idiomatic: The halls Ningcui, Zhaohe, Chongzhi, and Guangji, the Imperial Horse Stables, Bell and Drum Office, new Leopard Quarters buildings in the southern city, and the gunpowder depot were all rebuilt anew.

sentences.zh: 權幸閹宦莊園祠墓香火寺觀，工部復竊官銀以媚焉。

translations.literal: For favored eunuchs' estates, shrines, tombs, incense temples, and monasteries, the Works Ministry again embezzled official silver to flatter them.
translations.idiomatic: For favored eunuchs' estates, shrines, tombs, and temples, the Works Ministry embezzled official funds to curry favor.

sentences.zh: 給事中張原言：「工匠養父母妻子，尺籍之兵禦外侮，京營之軍衛王室，今奈何令民無所賴，兵不麗伍，利歸私門，怨叢公室乎？

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Yuan said: Artisans support parents, wives, and children; rostered soldiers repel foreign insult; capital-garrison troops guard the royal house—how now can the people have nothing to rely on, troops not fill their ranks, profit return to private doors, and resentment gather at the public office?
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Yuan said: "Artisans support families, rostered soldiers defend the frontier, and capital troops guard the throne—why leave the people destitute, ranks unfilled, profits in private hands, and public resentment mounting?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，謫貴州新添驛丞。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, he was demoted to courier station assistant in Xintian, Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial arrived, he was demoted to a courier post in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗營建最繁，十五年以前，名為汰省，而經費已六七百萬。

translations.literal: The Shizong's construction was most extensive; before the fifteenth year it was called trimming and saving, yet expenditures already reached six or seven million.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's construction was heaviest; before year 15 it was called austerity, yet costs already reached six or seven million taels.

sentences.zh: 其後增十數倍，齋宮、祕殿並時而興。

translations.literal: Afterward it increased tenfold and more; fasting palaces and secret halls rose at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Costs then rose more than tenfold as fasting palaces and secret halls sprang up together.

sentences.zh: 工廠二三十處，役匠數萬人，軍稱之，歲費二三百萬。

translations.literal: Work factories numbered twenty or thirty places, employing tens of thousands of artisans—called by the military—with annual cost of two or three million.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty or thirty workshops employed tens of thousands of artisans at an annual cost of two or three million taels.

sentences.zh: 其時宗廟、萬壽宮災，帝不之省，營繕益急。

translations.literal: At that time the ancestral temple and Wanshou Palace burned; the emperor did not reflect on it, and construction repair grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancestral temple and Wanshou Palace burned, the emperor took no heed and pressed construction harder.

sentences.zh: 經費不敷，乃令臣民獻助；

translations.literal: Funds were insufficient, so ministers and people were ordered to contribute aid;
translations.idiomatic: When funds ran short, officials and commoners were told to contribute;

sentences.zh: 獻助不已，復行開納。

translations.literal: contributions did not cease, and purchase-by-donation was again implemented.
translations.idiomatic: contributions continued, and purchase offices were opened again.

sentences.zh: 勞民耗財，視武宗過之。

translations.literal: Laboring the people and consuming wealth exceeded the Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Burden on the people and waste of wealth exceeded Wuzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 萬曆以後，營建織造，溢經制數倍，加以徵調、開採，民不得少休。

translations.literal: After Wanli, construction and weaving manufacture overflowed established regulations several times over; add requisitions and mining—the people could not rest even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanli construction and imperial workshops exceeded regulations several times over; with requisitions and mining, the people knew no rest.

sentences.zh: 迨閹人亂政，建第營墳，僭越亡等，功德私祠遍天下。

translations.literal: When eunuchs disturbed government, building mansions and tending tombs, transgressing ranks without measure, merit shrines and private temples spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs dominated politics, they built mansions and tombs beyond their rank, and private merit shrines spread empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 蓋二百餘年，民力殫殘久矣。

translations.literal: For more than two hundred years the people's strength had long been exhausted and crippled.
translations.idiomatic: For more than two centuries popular strength had been exhausted.

sentences.zh: 其以職役優免者，少者一二丁，多者至十六丁。

translations.literal: Those with preferential exemption through office and corvée: at least one or two males, at most up to sixteen males.
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders enjoying corvée exemption ranged from one or two males to as many as sixteen.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，免田有至二三千者。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period exempted fields reached two or three thousand in some cases.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli some exemptions covered two or three thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 至若賦稅蠲免，有恩蠲，有災蠲。

translations.literal: As for rent and tax exemption, there was grace exemption and disaster exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Tax exemptions took two forms: grace remissions and disaster remissions.

sentences.zh: 太祖之訓，凡四方水旱輒免稅，豐歲無災傷，亦擇地瘠民貧者優免之。

translations.literal: The Taizu's instruction: whenever the four directions had flood or drought, taxes were immediately exempted; in abundant years without disaster harm, those in poor land and poor people were also selectively given preferential exemption.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu ruled that flood or drought anywhere brought immediate tax exemption; even in good years the poor on marginal land received preferential relief.

sentences.zh: 凡歲災，盡蠲二稅，且貸以米，甚者賜米布若鈔。

translations.literal: Whenever there was annual disaster, both taxes were fully remitted, and grain was loaned; in severe cases grain, cloth, or paper notes were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In disaster years both taxes were fully remitted, grain was loaned, and in severe cases grain, cloth, or notes were granted outright.

sentences.zh: 又設預備倉，令老人運鈔易米以儲粟。

translations.literal: Reserve granaries were also established, ordering elders to transport paper notes to exchange for grain and store millet.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve granaries were established, with elders exchanging notes for grain to build stores.

sentences.zh: 荊、蘄水災，命戶部主事趙乾往振，遷延半載，怒而誅之。

translations.literal: When Jing and Qi suffered flood disaster, he ordered Ministry of Revenue section chief Zhao Gan to go for relief; he delayed half a year, and in anger the emperor executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Qi flooded, Revenue section chief Zhao Gan was sent to relieve distress but delayed half a year and was executed in the emperor's anger.

sentences.zh: 青州旱蝗，有司不以聞，逮治其官吏。

translations.literal: Qingzhou suffered drought and locusts; responsible offices did not report it, and their officials were arrested and punished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhou suffered drought and locusts, officials who failed to report it were arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 旱傷州縣，有司不奏，許耆民申訴，處以極刑。

translations.literal: In drought-stricken prefectures and counties, if responsible offices did not memorialize, elders were permitted to appeal, and extreme punishment was applied.
translations.idiomatic: In drought-stricken districts, if officials failed to report, elders could appeal and officials faced capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 孝感饑，其令請以預備倉振貸，帝命行人馳驛往，且諭戶部：自今凡歲饑，先發倉庾以貸，然後聞，著為令。

translations.literal: When Xiaogan suffered famine, its magistrate requested relief and loans from the reserve granary; the emperor ordered a traveling clerk to go by express relay and also instructed the Ministry of Revenue: From now on whenever there is annual famine, first issue granary grain for loans, then report—establish this as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaogan starved, its magistrate sought reserve-granary relief; the emperor sent a courier at once and told Revenue: "From now on, in famine years disburse granary grain first and report afterward"—codified as law.

sentences.zh: 」在位三十餘年，賜予布鈔數百萬，米百餘萬，所蠲租稅無數。

translations.literal: " During more than thirty years on the throne he bestowed several million in cloth and notes, more than a million in grain, and remitted rent and tax beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: " In thirty years on the throne he granted millions in cloth and notes, more than a million dan of grain, and remitted taxes beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 成祖聞河南饑，有司匿不以聞，逮沼之。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu heard of famine in Henan, responsible offices concealed it and did not report; he had them summoned and rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu learned Henan was starving but officials had concealed it, he summoned and rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 因命都御史陳瑛榜諭天下，有司水旱災傷不以聞者，罪不宥。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying to post notices throughout the realm: responsible offices that did not report flood, drought, or disaster harm would not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying to post notices empire-wide: officials who failed to report flood, drought, or disaster would not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 又敕朝廷歲遣巡視官，目擊民艱不言者，悉逮下獄。

translations.literal: He also ordered that each year the court send inspection officials; those who witnessed the people's hardship and did not speak were all arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered annual inspection tours: officials who witnessed hardship and remained silent were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 仁宗監國時，有以發振請者，遣人馳諭之，言：「軍民睏乏，待哺嗷嗷，尚從容啟請待報，不能效漢汲黯耶？

translations.literal: When the Renzong supervised the state, someone requested issuing relief; he sent a man by express relay to instruct him, saying: Soldiers and civilians are destitute and starving, crying for food—yet you still calmly memorialize and wait for reply? Cannot you emulate Han's Ji An?
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the state, Renzong heard a request to issue relief and sent word: "Soldiers and civilians starve and cry for food—will you only memorialize and wait? Cannot you act like Han's Ji An?"

sentences.zh: 」宣宗時，戶部請核饑民。

translations.literal: " In the Xuanzong's time the Ministry of Revenue requested verification of famine victims.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Xuanzong the Ministry of Revenue asked to verify famine victims.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「民饑無食，濟之當如拯溺救焚，奚待勘。

translations.literal: The emperor said: When the people starve without food, aiding them should be like saving the drowning and rescuing from fire—why wait for investigation?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When people starve, relief should be like saving someone from drowning or fire—why wait for an investigation?"

sentences.zh: 」蓋二祖、仁、宣時，仁政亟行。

translations.literal: " For in the times of the two founders, Ren, and Xuan, benevolent government was urgently practiced.
translations.idiomatic: " Under the two founders, Renzong, and Xuanzong, benevolent policies were pursued vigorously.

sentences.zh: 預備倉之外，又時時截起運，賜內帑。

translations.literal: Beyond reserve granaries, transport-out grain was also cut off from time to time and inner-treasury funds bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Besides reserve granaries, grain destined for transport was diverted and inner-treasury funds granted.

sentences.zh: 被災處無儲粟者，發旁縣米振之。

translations.literal: Where disaster-struck places had no stored grain, grain from neighboring counties was issued for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Where disaster areas lacked stores, neighboring counties' grain was released for relief.

sentences.zh: 蝗蝻始生，必遣人捕枌。

translations.literal: When locust nymphs first appeared, people were always sent to capture and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: When locust nymphs first appeared, officials were sent to destroy them at once.

sentences.zh: 鬻子女者，官為收贖。

translations.literal: Those selling sons and daughters—the state redeemed them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sold children were redeemed by the state.

sentences.zh: 且令富人蠲佃戶租。

translations.literal: The wealthy were also ordered to remit tenants' rent.
translations.idiomatic: The wealthy were ordered to remit tenants' rent.

sentences.zh: 大戶貸貧民粟，免其雜役為息，豐年償之。

translations.literal: Great households loaned grain to poor people, exempting miscellaneous corvée as interest, to be repaid in abundant years.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households loaned grain to the poor, accepting exemption from miscellaneous corvée as interest, repayable in good years.

sentences.zh: 皇莊、湖泊皆馳禁，聽民採取。

translations.literal: Imperial estates and lakes were all urgently opened, allowing the people to gather from them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial estates and lakes were opened for public gathering.

sentences.zh: 饑民還籍，給以口糧。

translations.literal: Famine refugees returning to registration were given ration grain.
translations.idiomatic: Famine refugees returning home received ration grain.

sentences.zh: 京、通倉米，平價出糶。

translations.literal: Capital and Tongzhou granary grain was sold at fair price.
translations.idiomatic: Grain from capital and Tongzhou granaries was sold at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 兼預給俸糧以殺米價，建官舍以處流民，給糧以收棄嬰，養濟院窮民各注籍，無籍者收養蠟燭、幡竿二寺。

translations.literal: Salary grain was also advanced to reduce grain price; official lodging was built to house refugees; grain was given to take in abandoned infants; poor people in relief hospices were each registered; those without registration were received at the Candle and Banner-Pole two temples.
translations.idiomatic: Salary grain was advanced to curb prices; lodging was built for refugees; grain funded adoption of abandoned infants; poorhouses registered the needy; the unregistered were sheltered at the Candle and Banner-Pole temples.

sentences.zh: 其恤民如此。

translations.literal: Their compassion for the people was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was their care for the people.

sentences.zh: 世宗、神宗於民事略矣，而災荒疏至，必賜蠲振，不敢違祖制也。

translations.literal: The Shizong and Shenzong were slight in civilian affairs, yet when disaster memorials arrived they always granted remission and relief, not daring to violate ancestral institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong and Shenzong neglected civilian welfare, yet when disaster reports arrived they still granted remissions and relief, not daring to break ancestral precedent.

sentences.zh: 振米之法，明初，大口六斗，小口三斗，五歲以下不與。

translations.literal: The method of relief grain: early Ming, adult mouths six dou, child mouths three dou, under five years not given.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming relief grain: six dou for adults, three for children, none under age five.

sentences.zh: 永樂以後，減其數。

translations.literal: After Yongle the amounts were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle the amounts were reduced.

sentences.zh: 納米振濟贖罪者，景帝時，雜犯死罪六十石，流徒減三之一，餘遞減有差。

translations.literal: Those paying grain for relief and redemption of offenses: in the Jingdi's time, miscellaneous capital offenses sixty dan, exile and penal servitude reduced by one-third, the rest progressively reduced by grades.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingdi, grain payment for relief and crime redemption required sixty dan for miscellaneous capital crimes, with exile and penal servitude reduced by one-third and lesser offenses reduced proportionally.

sentences.zh: 捐納事例，自憲宗始。

translations.literal: Contribution purchase precedents began with the Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Purchase-by-contribution precedents began under Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 生員納米百石以上，人國子監；

translations.literal: Students paying one hundred dan of grain or more entered the Imperial Academy;
translations.idiomatic: Students contributing one hundred dan or more of grain entered the Imperial Academy;

sentences.zh: 軍民納二百五十石，為正九品散官，加五十石，增二級，至正七品止。

translations.literal: soldiers and civilians paying two hundred fifty dan became ninth-rank regular honorary officials; adding fifty dan raised two grades, up to seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers and civilians paying 250 dan received ninth-rank honorary office; each additional 50 dan raised two grades, up to seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，富民納粟振濟，千石以上者表其門，九百石至二三百石者，授散官，得至從六品。

translations.literal: In the Wuzong's time wealthy households paying grain for relief: those of one thousand dan and above had their gates honored; from nine hundred down to two or three hundred dan, honorary offices were granted, reaching as high as vice sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuzong wealthy donors of relief grain: 1,000 dan or more earned honored gates; 900 down to 200–300 dan earned honorary office up to vice sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 世宗令義民出谷二十石者，給冠帶，多者授官正七品，至五百石者，有司為立坊。

translations.literal: The Shizong ordered that righteous people giving twenty dan of grain received cap and belt; more received seventh-rank office; up to five hundred dan, responsible offices erected a commemorative arch.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong granted cap and belt to donors of twenty dan; larger donors received seventh-rank office; at five hundred dan magistrates erected commemorative arches.

sentences.zh: 振粥之法，自世宗始。

translations.literal: The method of relief porridge began with the Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Relief porridge distribution began under Shizong.

sentences.zh: 報災之法，洪武時不拘時限。

translations.literal: The method of reporting disaster: in Hongwu there was no time limit.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster reporting under Hongwu had no time limit.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，始限夏災不得過五月終，秋災不得過九月終。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi limits were first set: summer disasters not past the end of the fifth month, autumn disasters not past the end of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi deadlines were set: summer disasters by end of month 5, autumn disasters by end of month 9.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，又分近地五月、七月，邊地七月、九月。

translations.literal: In Wanli it was further divided: nearby regions fifth and seventh months, frontier regions seventh and ninth months.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli nearby regions used months 5 and 7, frontier regions months 7 and 9.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，勘災既實，盡與蠲免。

translations.literal: In Hongwu, once disaster investigation was verified, all was remitted and exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, once disasters were verified, taxes were fully remitted.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，始定全災免七分，自九分災以下遞減。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi it was first fixed: total disaster exempted seven-tenths; from nine-tenths disaster downward, progressively reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi total disaster brought seventy-percent exemption, with lesser disasters reduced proportionally from ninety-percent downward.

sentences.zh: 又止免存留，不及起運，後遂為永制云。

translations.literal: Exemption also applied only to retained grain, not reaching transport-out; later this became permanent regulation, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Exemption applied only to locally retained grain, not transport quotas—a rule that later became permanent.
